data.title: Search could be so much better. And I don't mean chatbots with web access
data.author: mfkhalil
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种新型搜索引擎MatterRank，其核心特点是让用户能够控制搜索结果的排序，而不仅仅是让算法猜测用户的需求。传统的搜索引擎通过关键词、链接和各种信号来猜测用户意图，而MatterRank允许用户用自己的语言描述如何排序结果，提供更个性化和精准的搜索体验。这不是一个简单的聊天机器人或智能自动补全工具，而是一种全新的搜索方式，让用户决定什么最重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：搜索引擎的使用体验和功能改进

不同观点：
• [q0uaur] 认为该搜索引擎的概念不错，但怀疑其每次查询的成本较高。测试时要求排除大科技公司和广告，但结果中仍出现YouTube和Reddit，质疑算法是否真正过滤了域名。
• [maximumgeek] 批评该帖缺乏上下文，认为搜索结果仍需改进，尤其是广告和无用结果的过滤问题。对Quora答案和此类宣传帖感到厌烦。
• [SteveDavis88] 希望有一个能严格按照指定关键词返回结果的搜索引擎，认为谷歌无法满足这一点。
• [renegat0x0] 讨论了使用大型SQLite数据库进行域名搜索的可能性，但承认面临垃圾信息和过滤的挑战，类似于谷歌的处理方式。
• [danpalmer] 不同意搜索引擎假设用户不知道自己想要什么的说法，认为这是对搜索引擎体验的误解。
• [mfkhalil] 支持使用MatterRank，认为其能提供超越关键词匹配的定性特征结果，例如特定内容过滤，提供更高的搜索精度。
• [AymanJabr] 批评需要注册和创建引擎的步骤，希望直接使用搜索功能，不关心保存引擎供日后使用。
• [karmakaze] 质疑该帖是否为宣传广告，认为缺乏技术内容，未解释为何MatterRank优于Perplexity。
• [janalsncm] 认为使用LLM（大型语言模型）进行排名虽然结果质量较高，但速度较慢，建议通过过滤低质量内容和使用神经网络提高速度。
• [BrenBarn] 认为不仅是搜索引擎，现代技术普遍存在告诉用户该做什么的趋势，而非让用户自主决定。
• [eternauta3k] 质疑在每个结果上运行LLM的成本是否过高。
• [vivzkestrel] 提出Kagi与MatterRank的比较问题。
• [skeptrune] 询问是否存在某种交叉编码器用于评分提示。
• [TekMol] 坚决反对需要创建账户才能使用搜索引擎的做法。

补充讨论：
• 搜索结果的质量和相关性是主要关注点，尤其是广告和低质量内容的过滤。
• 用户普遍对需要注册或创建账户的搜索引擎持负面态度。
• 不同用户对LLM的使用持不同看法，有人认为能提高结果质量，有人认为速度太慢。
• 对MatterRank的功能和优势存在争议，部分用户质疑其宣传效果。
• 比较不同搜索引擎（如Kagi和MatterRank）的讨论显示用户对搜索引擎的选择和偏好存在差异。

43563915.article_content:
Search could be so much better
And I don't mean chatbots with access to a search engine.
Search is suffering from a quiet, unfortunate assumption. One that made the internet accessible to billions—but made it much less personal than it could be.
It assumes we don't know what we want.
This isn't search engines' fault. For decades, the only way we could communicate what we wanted was through a little search box.
So they did their best. They built systems to guess what we meant—ranking pages based on overlapping words, backlinks, reputation, and a hundred other signals. The best version of that became PageRank. And it was so good, it powered one of the most valuable companies in history.
But then computers learned how to understand language.
Now, we can do something new: we can tell search engines not just what we want, but
how we want it ranked
.
MatterRank is the first search engine where you control the ranking—using your own words.
This isn't a chatbot that summarizes results. And it's not just smarter autocomplete.
It's a new kind of search engine—one that lets you decide what matters most.
Let me know what you uncover. My email's below.
—Moe Khalil
Founder of MatterRank
moe@matterrank.ai
Try it now!
...or read more about how it works
→

data.title: Show HN: The C3 programming language (C alternative language)
data.author: lerno
data.article_summary: C3是一种基于C语言语法和语义的编程语言，旨在进化C语言的同时保持C程序员熟悉的特性。C3强调与C语言的ABI兼容性，可以轻松在同一项目中混合使用C和C3代码。其设计原则包括保持C语言的核心特性，仅在必要时进行修改，并引入一些高层次的便利功能。C3没有强制性的头文件，采用基于模块的命名空间，支持切片、编译时反射、增强的编译时执行、基于泛型模块的泛型编程、基于"Result"类型的零开销错误处理、延迟执行（defer）、值方法、关联枚举数据等特性。C3的灵感来源于C2语言，旨在迭代C语言而不是创造一种全新的语言。预编译的二进制文件适用于Windows x64、Debian x64、Ubuntu x86和MacOS Arm64等操作系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对C3编程语言的评价与讨论，包括语法、功能、与类似语言的对比以及对特定语言特性的需求和建议。

不同观点：
• [sfpotter] 认为使用 `::` 语法很丑陋，支持像D语言那样统一使用 `.`。他强调了简洁语法的重要性。
• [micklemeal] 实际使用后觉得C3在整合C库方面表现最好，尤其是与raylib和libtmx的整合，并对C3未来获得更多认可抱有期待。
• [dooglius] 提出C3与Zig、Odin的对比，这些语言都有改进C的相同目标，并质疑C3能否获得同样的关注。
• [Sohcahtoa82] 喜欢C3在switch/case行为上的改变，但对使用 `fn` 定义函数的必要性提出疑问，并表示如果需要用C语言时会考虑C3。

补充讨论：
• [dkersten] 对C3的整体印象积极，但对某些语法选择（如函数定义格式）有不同偏好，理解其设计背后的原因。
• [johnisgood] 关心标准库的贡献（如添加BLAKE2）以及如何使用不同的哈希算法实现“rehash”，并对线程安全的哈希表是否能进入标准库表示关注。
• [moktonar] 对使用 `fn` 标记函数定义的必要性提出疑问。
• [unclad5968] 使用C3后觉得不错，但希望有标记联合类型，并提到该特性已在计划中。
• [CyberDildonics] 认为系统语言应具备泛型、析构函数和所有权三个特性，而C3只具备泛型，对此表示遗憾。
• [accelbred] 关心是否能实现弱函数以及是否支持类似GCC的构造函数属性。
• [owlstuffing] 认为C3在处理宏和条件编译方面不够理想，质疑其设计选择。
• [djmips] 询问是否支持原生的定点类型。
• [alcover] 询问如何表达只读指针，类似于C语言中的 `const int* ptr`。
• [xormapmap] 认为许多C替代语言添加了过多复杂特性，主张C的改进版应保持简单，去除不必要的复杂性并改进C的设计缺陷。

争议焦点：
• 语法选择，尤其是 `::` 和 `fn` 的使用，部分开发者认为这些增加了不必要的复杂性。
• 与Zig、Odin等类似语言的对比，讨论C3能否脱颖而出。
• 对C3应具备哪些核心系统语言特性的不同看法，如是否需要所有权和析构函数。

这些讨论反映了开发者对C3的不同期望和需求，尤其是关于语言设计和功能实现的争议。

C3 Language
C3 is a programming language that builds on the syntax and semantics of the C language,
with the goal of evolving it while still retaining familiarity for C programmers.
It's an evolution, not a revolution: the C-like
for programmers who like C.
Precompiled binaries for the following operating systems are available:
Windows x64
download
,
install instructions
.
Debian x64
download
,
install instructions
.
Ubuntu x86
download
,
install instructions
.
MacOS Arm64
download
,
install instructions
.
The manual for C3 can be found at
www.c3-lang.org
.
Thanks to full ABI compatibility with C, it's possible to mix C and C3 in the same project with no effort. As a demonstration, vkQuake was compiled with a small portion of the code converted to C3 and compiled with the c3c compiler. (The fork can be found at
https://github.com/c3lang/vkQuake
)
Design Principles
Procedural "get things done"-type of language.
Try to stay close to C - only change what's really necessary.
C ABI compatibility and excellent C integration.
Learning C3 should be easy for a C programmer.
Data is inert.
Avoid "big ideas" & the "more is better" fallacy.
Introduce some higher level conveniences where the value is great.
C3 owes its inspiration to the
C2 language
: to iterate on top of C without trying to be a
whole new language.

generic modules
(more examples can be found at
https://c3-lang.org/references/docs/examples/
).

In what ways does C3 differ from C?
No mandatory header files
New semantic macro system
Module based name spacing
Slices
Compile time reflection
Enhanced compile time execution
Generics based on generic modules
"Result"-based zero overhead error handling
Defer
Value methods
Associated enum data
No preprocessor

主要讨论点：如何有效检测和应对网络游戏中的作弊行为，以及作弊行为对游戏和玩家的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持实名认证和严厉惩罚**：

  - [thesuitonym]: 同样不理解作弊者为何会反复使用作弊手段，认为这破坏了游戏的乐趣。

  - [ultimafan]: 提到队友明知有人作弊却不采取行动，可能是因为从作弊中获益而不感到内疚。
  - [nathants]: 提出单人模式游戏可以避免指责队友，并讨论了各种反作弊技术的必要性。

  - [trod1234]: 对作弊者进行严厉的道德批判，认为他们是人类的祸害，故意无视自己的破坏性行为，需要被制止。

补充讨论：
• **市场和游戏环境的恶化**：
  - [kibwen]: 希望不可阻挡的作弊手段能摧毁依赖随机队友和对手的竞争性在线游戏子类型市场。
  - [twic]: 提出一种自我保护策略，即通过表现差劲来避免被作弊者盯上。

• **社会反应和治理**：
  - [creddit]: 提出社会缺乏对作弊行为的免疫机制，使得公开创建作弊软件的人未被排斥，感到这是社会的悲哀。

争议焦点：
• 实名认证和隐私之间的平衡问题，部分玩家不愿意为游戏提供身份信息。
• 作弊行为的道德性质和应采取的惩罚措施，特别是作弊对游戏社区的长期影响。

43574929.article_content:
niila.fi
<- Posts
Posted: 2025-04-03
AI cheats: why you didn’t notice your teammate was cheating
For the past few years, cheats have evolved rapidly. First came memory reading aimbots, then colorbots, and now AI aim assist. Cheats have escaped the host PC. How does it affect the players and anti-cheats?
vike256
That's me, or the handle that I use online. I've been in the video game hacking scene on and off for what seems like forever. I don't know the exact point when I stumbled upon it, but I was making my first cheats on my Android phone when I was 12.
I didn't have a PC at the time, so I sat on my bed with a rooted phone in my hands that had GameGuardian installed. I remember writing a trainer with Lua for a game called Growtopia. I've since gotten a PC and programmed a few more cheats. Most notably Unibot, an open-source colorbot.
[1]
Image of Unibot debug screen while detecting an enemy. Green box is the detection area. Red box is the target.
Read more
Colorbots, why they work... or don’t
Colorbots read the enemy positions from the screen. They scan every pixel and filter based on enemy colors. It works for games that have colored enemy highlights or outlines.
Their flaw is that they don't work in every game, and they can merge multiple enemies into a single target if they are too close together. This can lock the cheater’s aim between enemies, unable to shoot either.
Image of someone having issues with multiple enemies merging into a single target. The user seems to be using Unibot.
The post
Colorbots became popular as the first cheats to achieve aimbot without memory reading. Colorbots are quite hard to detect. You can essentially just plug in a capture card to your PC and pass the images to another PC that the cheat runs on.
The aimbot input can be sent along with your normal mouse input through an Arduino or a KMBox. Just plug the KMBox to your PC and connect both the cheat PC and your mouse to it.
Diagram of how a 2PC cheat could function. This would work for both AI and colorbot cheats.
AI cheats are essentially advanced colorbots
Colorbots don't work on all games, because not all games have distinct enemy colors. This is where AI comes in. Developers train AI models to detect enemies, then distribute these models to users. This makes a single cheat work on every game imaginable.
So, the host PC only has a capture card and a "mouse" plugged into it, and the second PC runs the cheat. The anti-cheat has no idea, and...
You have no idea
You probably won’t notice the cheat while spectating, because cheat developers are intentionally nerfing their cheats to evade detection. Anti-cheats have made cheats more expensive, time-consuming, and less effective.
Today's cheats cost more but do less. Now a typical cheater needs an extra PC, external hardware, and $5-500 monthly payments just to bypass a decent anti-cheat.
After all that, they are still at a risk of getting banned. Cheaters must reflash their BIOS, wipe their PCs, reinstall Windows, and create a new account to play again. That's not something I'd like to do once a few weeks.
Cats seems to be the most helpful bunch among cheater forums.
So you being unable to spot a slight aim assist while spectating is normal. Of course you'll notice the aim assist if the player is insanely bad and has the aimbot configured wrong, but that's just plain stupidity being witnessed.
[1] Unibot is an open-source colorbot I made late 2023. It was not the first of its kind but it made waves within the cheating community. It was the first user-friendly, modifiable colorbot compatible with games like Valorant, Overwatch, and Roblox.
...yes Roblox. It has many FPS games that people play. Bad Business and Rivals are my favorites, but most people seemed to use Unibot for Arsenal. Unibot had a config file that you could use to change the important values. It was the first time users would not have to touch code to make the cheat work on their favourite game.
Unibot is still available on my GitHub. If you’re interested, check out the
GitHub Wiki
. The documentation is quite good for a game cheat.

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：mRNA疫苗研究的联邦资助前景及相关科学问题

不同观点：
• [对研究资助受阻的担忧] ceejayoz 指出，联邦对mRNA疫苗研究的支持可能因官员的干涉而陷入危机，尤其是健康秘书Robert F. Kennedy Jr.对疫苗持反对态度，可能影响研究进展。
• [个体化治疗的疑问] tqi 提问，mRNA治疗是否需要根据个体定制靶向肽，还是具有普遍适用性。这反映了对mRNA技术在具体应用中的个性化需求缺乏了解。
• [研究内容的相关性] bookofjoe 表达了对过去发表涉及小鼠而非人类的研究文章的疑虑，提到因为经常看到评论关注“在小鼠中有效”而感到疲惫，暗示对研究成果在人类中的适用性存在担忧。

补充讨论：
• [对科学机构的质疑] pwdiscflatmajor 以讽刺语气提出“科学和美国科学促进会（AAAS）是杀手？”，可能是在质疑科学机构的动机或其对某些研究的支持。
• [临床应用的时间] fnord77 关注mRNA疫苗技术何时能进入临床应用，反映了公众对研究进展和实际医疗应用之间时间差的关注。
• [实验对象的局限性] moffkalast 简短评论“in mice”，进一步强调了许多研究仅在小鼠模型中有效，而尚未在人类中得到验证，暗示对研究成果转化到临床应用的怀疑。

争议焦点：
• 联邦资助削减和政治干预是否会实质性影响mRNA疫苗研究的进展，以及这种干预的合理性。
• mRNA技术在个体化治疗中的适用性，以及从小鼠实验到人类临床应用的转化过程中的不确定性。

data.title: Show HN: GitMCP is an automatic MCP server for every GitHub repo
data.author: liadyo
data.article_summary: GitMCP 是一个能够为任何 GitHub 项目创建远程 MCP 服务器的工具。通过将 GitHub 项目 URL 中的 "github.com" 或 "github.io" 替换为 "gitmcp.io"，用户可以为 AI 助手提供更准确的代码上下文信息，提升其回应的准确性和相关性。GitMCP 支持读取代码仓库中的文件如 llms.txt、llms-full.txt 和 readme.md，并能与 GitHub Pages 及任何公开的 GitHub 仓库无缝协作。设置简单，兼容 Claude、Cursor、Windsurf 和 VSCode Insiders 等主流 MCP 兼容的 AI 工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitMCP项目的功能、实现、应用场景及技术细节

不同观点：
• [kiitos] 对GitMCP的实际工作原理感到困惑，尤其是其具体实现和限制。他认为项目的着陆页缺乏足够的文档说明，没有解释MCP协议的具体实现细节，也没有说明如何解析和转换数据。
• [sivaragavan] 认为GitMCP项目是个好的开始，但目前实用性不强。他提到项目创建的两个工具中，一个工具未能正常工作，但另一个工具成功获取了文档。他表示对这个项目的未来可能性感兴趣。
• [ianpurton] 提供了关于LLM（大语言模型）和MCP协议如何结合使用的技术背景，解释了LLM如何通过调用函数来获取代码信息，并认为GitMCP可以在这个过程中发挥作用。
• [liadyo] 介绍了GitMCP的开源远程MCP服务器，解释了如何通过替换URL访问GitHub项目的文档，并提供了项目链接。
• [the_arun] 对GitMCP的应用场景表示不理解，质疑为什么需要为GitHub仓库设置MCP服务器。
• [pcwelder] 建议使用一个MCP服务器，通过工具调用参数来处理不同的仓库路径或URL，以减少配置的麻烦。
• [qwertox] 关注GitMCP在私有仓库和简单实现上的局限性，并建议提供Dockerfile以便于本地运行。
• [xena] 询问如何选择退出GitMCP对个人仓库的服务。
• [fzysingularity] 认为GitMCP没有充分利用MCP的状态特性，建议增强Git仓库与MCP的集成，使其更具状态性和交互性。
• [creddit] 质疑GitMCP与参考MCP服务器的区别，认为在已有参考服务器的情况下，选择自托管服务器可能不太明智。
• [eagleinparadise] 报告了在Cursor中使用GitMCP时遇到的错误，并询问是否可以强制使用MCP服务器。
• [lukew3] 对项目名称提出建议，认为当前名称可能引起混淆，建议改为更明确的描述。
• [fallat] 对MCP的快速发展表示惊讶和赞赏。
• [thomasfromcdnjs] 对项目表示赞赏和支持。

补充讨论：
• 项目的实用性和当前功能实现的有效性存在争议，部分用户认为项目尚不成熟，功能有限。
• 用户对MCP服务器在私有仓库和简单实现上的支持提出质疑，并建议改进文档和配置方式。
• 部分用户对项目的技术细节和应用场景表示困惑，尤其是MCP的具体实现和优势。
• 项目名称可能引起混淆，有用户建议更改名称以避免误解。

What is Hatchet?
Hatchet is a platform for running background tasks, built on top of Postgres. Instead of managing your own task queue or pub/sub system, you can use Hatchet to distribute your functions between a set of workers with minimal configuration or infrastructure.
When should I use Hatchet?
Background tasks are critical for offloading work from your main web application. Usually background tasks are sent through a FIFO (first-in-first-out) queue, which helps guard against traffic spikes (queues can absorb a lot of load) and ensures that tasks are retried when your task handlers error out. Most stacks begin with a library-based queue backed by Redis or RabbitMQ (like Celery or BullMQ). But as your tasks become more complex, these queues become difficult to debug, monitor and start to fail in unexpected ways.
This is where Hatchet comes in. Hatchet is a full-featured background task management platform, with built-in support for chaining complex tasks together into workflows, alerting on failures, making tasks more durable, and viewing tasks in a real-time web dashboard.
Features
📥 Queues
Hatchet is built on a durable task queue that enqueues your tasks and sends them to your workers at a rate that your workers can handle. Hatchet will track the progress of your task and ensure that the work gets completed (or you get alerted), even if your application crashes.
This is particularly useful for:
Ensuring that you never drop a user request
Flattening large spikes in your application
Breaking large, complex logic into smaller, reusable tasks

主要讨论点：伺服电机的技术原理、实际应用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [viraptor] 认为文章没有深入解释伺服电机的工作原理。他指出，文章只介绍了控制信号和伺服电机的响应结果，但缺少脉冲如何被转换、反馈机制如何工作以及安全机制等关键技术细节。

• [arbitrandomuser] 分享了一个黑客改造的视频链接，展示了如何让玩具伺服电机具有更高的精度和可重复性，但没有详细讨论技术细节。

• [Animats] 提到文章讨论的是1970年代的无线电控制玩具伺服电机，指出这些早期设备缺乏反馈输出，但仍然在低端机械输出设备中占主导地位，语气中带有不满。

• [dcrazy] 对电子元件分销商（如Jameco、Mouser等）提供大量入门教育文章的现象表示疑惑，推测这可能是为了SEO（搜索引擎优化），但同时质疑在这样一个相对小众的领域是否有必要这样做。

• [bilsbie] 提出一个基础问题，询问伺服电机如何保持其位置，以及这是否需要能量，关注的是电机工作的基本原理。

• [mkarliner] 对文章内容的真实性提出质疑，怀疑文章可能是由AI生成的。

• [brcmthrowaway] 分享了自己使用 hobby 伺服电机的实际体验，提到该电机产生高分贝的刺耳噪音，并询问有哪些更好的伺服电机选择。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术细节包括伺服电机的工作原理、反馈机制和安全机制，部分用户（如viraptor）对这些内容的缺失表示不满。
• 实际应用中的问题也被提及，例如伺服电机的噪音问题（brcmthrowaway）以及低端设备在市场中的持续存在（Animats）。
• 关于文章本身的质疑（mkarliner）和分销商SEO策略的讨论（dcrazy）为次要讨论点，但仍具有一定参考价值。

data.title: Declarative Schemas for simpler database management
data.author: kiwicopple
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了声明式 schema 如何简化复杂数据库的管理。声明式 schema 将数据库的最终期望状态存储在 `.sql` 文件中，便于集中管理和版本控制。相比直接修改数据库 schema，声明式 schema 具有以下优势：单一管理界面，减少冗余和错误；版本化迁移，确保不同环境中的一致性；简明的代码审查，无需重复复杂迁移脚本。

随着数据库 schema 复杂性增加，传统迁移方法难以维护，因为缺乏单一的整体视图。例如，在 Supabase 中，复杂的 `projects` 表涉及私有表、RLS（行级安全）、视图和触发器，修改时需多步操作，容易导致冲突。

声明式 schema 通过集中管理 schema，简化了开发流程，提高了开发效率。

不同观点：
• [xyzzy_plugh] 认为应该使用声明式 schema，但自动生成迁移脚本不可取。他建议手写迁移脚本并验证 schema 变化，通过测试确保数据库 schema 与预期一致。
• [jackb4040] 指出 SQL 本质上是命令式的语言，无法保证 create_table 等命令的安全执行。他强调声明式 schema 文件（schema file）的重要性，而不是依赖 SQL 命令。
• [webster451] 表示声明式 API 在某些场景下是有价值的，但大多数情况下，程序员需要对变更的控制以获得更好的行为。他认为世界本质上是命令式的，提供更高的控制和可预测性。
• [bartvk] 总结新的方法是直接修改 CREATE TABLE 脚本，工具自动计算差异并应用更改，这消除了新数据库创建和现有数据库更新之间的区别。

- 关于迁移脚本的编辑自由度和特定数据库操作的实现方法。
- 各种工具和方法在实际开发中的优缺点和取舍。

Declarative Schemas for Simpler Database Management
03 Apr 2025
•
7 minute read
Qiao Han
Engineering
Today we’re releasing declarative schemas to simplify managing and maintaining complex database schemas. With declarative schemas, you can define your database structure in a clear, centralized, and version-controlled manner.
What are declarative schemas?
#
Declarative schemas store the final desired state of the database in
.sql
files that can be saved and versioned alongside a project. For example, here is the declarative schema for a classic
products
table:
_
10
create table "products" (
_
10
"id" serial primary key,
_
10
"name" text not null,
_
10
"description" text,
_
10
"price" numeric(10,2) not null,
_
10
"created_at" timestamp default now()
_
10
);
_
10
_
10
alter table "products"
_
10
enable row level security;
Declarative schemas offer numerous benefits over making changes to your database schema directly:
Single pane of glass
. Maintain your entire database schema in one place, reducing redundancy and potential errors.
Versioned migrations
. Automatically generate migration files, ensuring consistent schema updated across environments. Store your declarative schema files alongside your project files in your version control system.
Concise code reviews
. Easily review changes to tables, views, and functions without manually repeating complex migration scripts.
Declarative schemas vs migrations
#
It's best practice to use
Migrations
to track and apply changes to databases. Every time you make a change, you create a new new file with all the changes, keeping changes versioned and reproducible.
However, as the complexity of a database schemas grows, it becomes increasingly difficult to develop using versioned migrations as there isn't a single place to see the entire database schema.
For example, at Supabase we have a complex and frequently-updated
projects
table. Here's partially what it looks like with RLS enabled:
_
32
create table private.projects (
_
32
id              bigint    not null,
_
32
name            text      not null,
_
32
organization_id bigint    not null,
_
32
inserted_at     timestamp not null,
_
32
updated_at      timestamp not null
_
32
);
_
32
_
32
alter table private.projects
_
32
enable row level security;
_
32
_
32
create policy projects_insert
_
32
on private.projects
_
32
for insert
_
32
to authenticated
_
32
with check auth.can_write(project_id);
_
32
_
32
create policy projects_select
_
32
on private.projects
_
32
for select
_
32
to authenticated
_
32
using auth.can_read(project_id);
_
32
_
32
-- Users can only view the projects that they have access to
_
32
create view public.projects as select
_
32
projects.id,
_
32
projects.name,
_
32
projects.organization_id,
_
32
projects.inserted_at,
_
32
projects.updated_at
_
32
from private.projects
_
32
where auth.can_read(projects.id);
The
projects
table is created in a private schema, with a public view exposed for reads. Attribute-based access control (ABAC) is implemented on top of RLS policies to ensure queries only return projects that the user has access to.
Since Postgres views are not updatable by default, we have defined trigger functions to cascade writes to the underlying table when a Supabase user creates a new project. This makes development easier because the
projects
view can be inserted with regular PostgREST calls while invoking the appropriate RLS policies on the underlying table.
_
24
-- Triggers to update views from PostgREST: select('projects').insert({ ... })
_
24
create function public.public_projects_on_insert() returns trigger
_
24
as $$
_
24
begin
_
24
insert into private.projects(
_
24
name,
_
24
organization_id,
_
24
inserted_at,
_
24
updated_at
_
24
) values (
_
24
NEW.name,
_
24
NEW.organization_id,
_
24
coalesce(NEW.inserted_at, now()),
_
24
coalesce(NEW.updated_at, now())
_
24
) returning * into NEW;
_
24
return NEW;
_
24
end
_
24
$$ language plpgsql;
_
24
_
24
create trigger public_projects_on_insert
_
24
instead of insert
_
24
on public.projects
_
24
for each row
_
24
execute function public.public_projects_on_insert();
This complexity slows down development velocity, as changes to the table might break other views or functions. Back in early 2022, a simple change to add a new column involved the following steps.
Find the latest schema for
projects
table in our migration files or by querying our database.
Write the
alter table
statement in a new migration file.
Copy and update the
projects
view definition to include the new column.
Copy and update the trigger function definition to include the new column.
Add new pgTAP tests and verify that existing tests pass.
Submit the new migration file for review, which would be at least a few hundred lines.
This process is tedious and it's frustrating to have multiple engineers working on the
projects
table concurrently. Merging PRs would result in a merge conflict that must be resolved by repeating steps 1-5.
Using declarative schemas in product

data.title: Was Houdini a Spy? (2021)
data.author: carlos-menezes
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了著名魔术师哈里·胡迪尼是否曾从事间谍活动。胡迪尼以其逃脱魔术和 illusionist 技巧闻名，他的技术不仅影响了魔术界，也对情报和间谍活动产生了深远影响。文章提到，中央情报局（CIA）曾聘请魔术师约翰·穆赫兰，在冷战期间教授特工欺骗技术，这些技术部分源于胡迪尼的魔术。穆赫兰为CIA编写的手册在1973年被下令销毁，但后来被部分恢复并出版为《CIA官方诡计与欺骗手册》。胡迪尼的隐藏工具和逃脱技巧被认为启发了二战和冷战时期的间谍设备。一些历史学家，如《胡迪尼的秘密生活》的作者，认为胡迪尼可能参与了情报工作，包括向德国和英国警方提供信息以及协助美国特勤局打击伪钞。然而，胡迪尼是否真的是间谍仍无定论。

• [ggm] 对Jasper Maskelyne的评价存在争议，认为他的战争记录有争议，并将他的形象比作“胡萝卜有助于夜视”的宣传手段，暗示其作用被夸大。
• [neilv] 引用了MKULTRA项目的历史背景，批评文章没有提及CIA过去的负面事件，认为在当前时刻不应模糊过去的教训，强调需要警惕政府内部滥用权力。

争议焦点：
• 对Jasper Maskelyne的评价存在分歧，一方认为其作用被夸大，另一方则可能认可其技能在特定历史背景下的价值。

整体讨论展示了魔术师与间谍活动的交集，并触及了历史事件中的道德和政治争议。

The worldâs most famous magician, Harry Houdini, was known as a celebrity conjurer, a practitioner of escape magic, and a master illusionist. Heâs had an enduring legacy on the magical arts since his untimely demise on Halloween Day, 1926. Thatâs why October 31
st
is known in magical circles as âNational Magic Dayâ or simply âHoudini Day.â
In honor of this legendary magician, weâre exploring the effect magic, and even Houdini, has had in the realms of intelligence and espionage.
Harry Houdini, courtesy of the Library of Congress
It may surprise people to learn that Houdiniâs magical techniques have influenced generations of clandestine officers. We even had a former CIA deputy director who was a magician himself!
But was Houdini more than just an influential figure?
Was he ever a practitioner in the art of espionage?
Was he a spy?
To answer these questions, we must first delve into the mystery of the missing magic manuals of Langley and the CIAâs first magician, John Mulholland.
Vintage poster for Harry Houdini show, courtesy of the Library of Congress.
Magic and Espionage at CIA
âMagic and espionage are really kindred arts,â or so wrote former CIA Deputy Director McLaughlin, an amateur magician himself, in the forward to the book, âThe Official C.I.A. Manual of Trickery and Deceptionâ by H. Keith Melton and Robert Wallace.
This book, created from two long-lost training guides designed to teach Agency officers how to integrate elements of the magicianâs craft into clandestine operations, revealed that the CIAâs connection to the world of magic was decades old.
In the 1950s, as part of the MKULTRA project, the Agency hired magician John Mulholland to teach young officers techniques of deception suitable for the field, such as smuggling assets out of East Germany during the Cold War in vehicles that resembled the magic boxes used in stage illusions.
As part of his contract, Mulholland prepared two training manuals; âSome Operational Applications of the Art of Deceptionâ and âRecognition Signals.â
In 1973, when then-CIA Director Richard Helms ordered the destruction of all documents associated with the MKULTRA program, the manuals were thought to be gone forever.
Then, in 2007 while going through some unrelated documents, Robert Wallace, a former director of the CIAâs Office of Technical Services, discovered references to the manuals and tracked down poor-quality copies of each that had somehow escaped the shredder.
Believing that the manuals merited publication in full, Wallace conferred with his co-author, intelligence historian and collector Keith Melton, to produce âThe Official C.I.A. Manual of Trickery and Deception,â which included illustrations of stage deception techniques, such as Harry Houdiniâs walk through a wall.
In fact, many of Houdiniâs magical escape techniques are discussed in the now declassified manuals, as they have influenced later generations of clandestine officers as well as spy gadgetry developed during the Cold War.
According to the Trickery and Deception book, concealment devises like magic coins and the hollow Mokana shoe used by Houdini for hiding escape tools became popular among spies throughout the Cold War era.
Even the Office of Strategic Services, the CIAâs WWII predecessor, was inspired by Houdini when they created tiny tools that mirrored those first used by the magician in his concealed escape kits.
Itâs no wonder then that many historians of magic and intelligence have found themselves pondering the question: Was Harry Houdiniâ¦
a spy?
Hungarian born magician and escapologist Harry Houdini (1874 – 1926) being fitted into an escape proof suit.   (Photo by MPI/Getty Images)
The Master of Deception, Harry Houdini
Since Houdiniâs death, there has been an on-going debate among historians as to whether or not Houdini was ever a âspy.â
The greatestÂ and most recent kerfuffle was theÂ publication in 2006 of âThe Secret Life of Houdini: The Making of Americaâs First Superheroâ by William Kalush and Larry Sloman, who conducted exhaustive research into the history of magic, eventually creating a fully text-searchable database of 700,000 pages of material, which contains thousands of references to Houdini.
Kalush and Sloman posit that the only reason Houdini would abruptly leave the United States in 1900, when he had finally achieved notorietyâand a paycheck equivalent to $45,000 a weekâwas because he was engaged in espionage. Houdini was rumored to be providing the German police with information about wanted criminals, as well as unspecified information to Scotland Yard Superintendent William Melville, monitoring anarchists in Russia, and helping the U.S. Secret Service with their anti-counterfeiting mission.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软的历史、产品质量、竞争行为及其在科技行业的地位

不同观点：
• **微软的竞争行为和产品质量差**：Jamie Zawinski（引用自warmandsoft）认为微软的商业行为具有掠夺性和反竞争性，并且其产品一直很糟糕。他个人对微软有成见，并呼吁其他人也不要使用微软的产品。

• **微软命名的巧合与历史机遇**：Taniwha提到在大学时期，他们团队曾为6800s编写编译器，并使用了“uSoft”这个名称（希腊字母mu），后来发现美国有人使用相同的名字。他对此表示遗憾，认为如果当时注册公司，可能能将名字卖个好价钱。

• **开源社区与微软的相互影响**：rollcat提到比尔·盖茨的《致爱好者的一封公开信》发表近50年，开源社区对软件行业的巨大影响，以及微软如何依赖这些工作。他还提到艺术创作中的“借鉴”是重要的过程。

• **微软办公环境与产品设计**：hnthrowaway0315对一个开发环境图片表示好奇，质疑为什么有两个架子，并提到微软员工曾经拥有独立办公室的印象。

• **产品质量与公司命运**：bustling-noose认为，尽管微软的大部分收入不再依赖Windows，但Windows的质量问题可能会影响公司的声誉，类似于谷歌搜索对谷歌公司的影响。

• **怀旧与技术进步**：0xEF表达了对过去技术简洁性的怀念，但也承认微软在世界上做了一些好事。

• **Windows 95的重大影响**：finnjohnsen2回忆起第一次看到Windows 95启动时的震撼，认为这是一个 stepping into the future 的时刻。

• **微软的人性化历程**：ErigmolCt指出，微软的旅程不仅是产品和商业里程碑，还包括人性化的经历，如在 Honda Civic 中招聘和与 Rolling Stones 谈判。

• **Windows 95的趣味性**：nocarrier提到Windows 95安装光盘中包含Weezer的Buddy Holly视频，认为这很酷。

• **微软相关书籍的评价**：phendrenad2推荐了一些关于早期微软的书籍，并对某些书的趣味性与信息量进行了评价。

补充讨论：
• **微软在游戏产业的影响**：brcmthrowaway简单提到没有微软就没有《半条命》这款游戏。

争议焦点：
• 微软的商业行为是否具有掠夺性和反竞争性，以及其产品质量是否如批评者所言如此糟糕，这是评论中一个潜在的争议点。

data.title: Microsoft reports several bootloader vulnerabilities
data.author: hacknslack
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软在安全领域的作用、开源与闭源系统的安全性、引导加载程序（bootloader）的安全性及改进建议

不同观点：
• [fuzzfactor] 认为微软应该利用其资源和AI技术，改进NT引导程序，使其无需Grub即可引导Linux，从而提高PC用户的安全性。他期待微软通过Windows Update发布相关安全补丁，并希望微软迅速行动。
• [zelon88] 对微软利用AI发现竞争对手产品漏洞的做法持批评态度，认为这是不厚道的行为。
• [usr1106] 指出Grub因其体积庞大而易于出现安全漏洞，建议使用更小、更安全的引导程序如systemd-boot。他还质疑微软是否会开放其源代码以供漏洞搜索。
• [greatgib] 批评“安全启动”（secure boot）的安全性，认为由于微软对操作系统签名的控制，拥有微软证书密钥的人可以为所欲为。他还提到许多平台仍在使用泄露的密钥。
• [moktonar] 推测微软可能已经发现了自己引导加载程序中的严重漏洞并悄悄修复了。
• [aaronmdjones] 指出文章中关于U-Boot CVE-2025-26729链接的不准确性，怀疑文章由AI生成。
• [ncr100] 对微软支持开源操作系统实践表示赞赏，并认为这增加了对开源操作系统的信任，但也暗示可能存在反垄断策略。
• [jonathanstrange] 认为能够绕过安全启动是一种特性而非缺陷，暗示该功能有其合理性。
• [neuroelectron] 认为通用引导加载程序并非安全目标，建议为特定硬件开发专门的引导加载程序，或者集成经过优化的硬件专用引导加载程序。

补充讨论：
• 微软是否应该开放其源代码以提高透明度和安全性是一个争议焦点。
• 对“安全启动”机制的信任问题，特别是涉及微软签名和密钥管理的漏洞，引起了关注。
• 不同用户对引导加载程序的体积和专用性有不同看法，有人认为小型或硬件专用引导加载程序更安全。
• 文章中链接不准确和可能由AI生成的问题引发了对信息可靠性的讨论。

data.title: Bash-ini-parser: Advanced bash INI parser library
data.author: lsferreira42
data.article_summary: Bash INI Parser 是一个用于解析和操作 INI 配置文件的 Bash 脚本库。它支持读写 INI 文件的值、列出文件中的段和键、添加、更新和删除段和键，以及处理复杂值（包括引号、空格和特殊字符）。该库还支持数组、在文件和环境变量之间导入导出数据，并具有详细的错误处理和调试模式。通过设置环境变量，可以自定义库的行为，如启用调试模式、严格验证段和键名等。安装时只需将 `lib_ini.sh` 脚本包含在项目中并导入即可使用。该库提供了多种功能，包括默认值获取、键存在性检查和配置选项设置等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对复杂Shell脚本的重写建议以及处理INI文件的工具选择

不同观点：
• [theamk的观点] 认为当Shell脚本变得过于复杂时，应该用"真正的编程语言"重写，推荐使用仅依赖标准库（stdlib）的Python。理由是Python的标准库功能齐全，包含INI文件解析器，且Python通常容易安装，尽管代码可能更冗长，但会更可靠和易于调试。

• [pixelbeat的观点] 提出可以使用专门处理INI文件的工具，如crudini，这是为Shell脚本设计的实用工具，能够有效处理INI文件。

• [rastignack的观点] 建议在持续集成/持续交付（CICD）环境中，可以使用Git来解析INI文件，因为Git在这种环境中通常已经存在。

• [cryptonector的观点] 建议使用INI到JSON的转换器加上jq工具来处理INI文件，认为这样就足够了。

• [IshKebab的观点] 认为这种复杂的Shell脚本或软件本身可能就是一个"错误"，表示如果使用这种软件，说明在设计上已经犯了重大错误。

补充讨论：
• [albert_e的观点] 离题地提到一个将印度语言引入现代技术的项目BHASHINI，因为名称相似而联想到该讨论中的"语言"问题。

争议焦点：对于处理复杂Shell脚本和INI文件的最佳工具和方法存在不同看法。theamk主张用Python重写以提高可靠性和可调试性，而pixelbeat、rastignack和cryptonextor则推荐使用特定工具或现有工具（如crudini、Git、jq）来简化处理过程。IshKebab的观点则质疑使用复杂脚本的必要性。

43539892.article_summary: Bash INI Parser 是一个用于解析和操作 INI 配置文件的 Bash 脚本库。它支持读写 INI 文件的值、列出文件中的段和键、添加、更新和删除段和键，以及处理复杂值（包括引号、空格和特殊字符）。该库还支持数组、在文件和环境变量之间导入导出数据，并具有详细的错误处理和调试模式。通过设置环境变量，可以自定义库的行为，如启用调试模式、严格验证段和键名等。安装时只需将 `lib_ini.sh` 脚本包含在项目中并导入即可使用。该库提供了多种功能，包括默认值获取、键存在性检查和配置选项设置等。
43539892.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对复杂Shell脚本的重写建议以及处理INI文件的工具选择

不同观点：
• [theamk的观点] 认为当Shell脚本变得过于复杂时，应该用"真正的编程语言"重写，推荐使用仅依赖标准库（stdlib）的Python。理由是Python的标准库功能齐全，包含INI文件解析器，且Python通常容易安装，尽管代码可能更冗长，但会更可靠和易于调试。

• [pixelbeat的观点] 提出可以使用专门处理INI文件的工具，如crudini，这是为Shell脚本设计的实用工具，能够有效处理INI文件。

• [rastignack的观点] 建议在持续集成/持续交付（CICD）环境中，可以使用Git来解析INI文件，因为Git在这种环境中通常已经存在。

• [cryptonector的观点] 建议使用INI到JSON的转换器加上jq工具来处理INI文件，认为这样就足够了。

• [IshKebab的观点] 认为这种复杂的Shell脚本或软件本身可能就是一个"错误"，表示如果使用这种软件，说明在设计上已经犯了重大错误。

补充讨论：
• [albert_e的观点] 离题地提到一个将印度语言引入现代技术的项目BHASHINI，因为名称相似而联想到该讨论中的"语言"问题。

争议焦点：对于处理复杂Shell脚本和INI文件的最佳工具和方法存在不同看法。theamk主张用Python重写以提高可靠性和可调试性，而pixelbeat、rastignack和cryptonextor则推荐使用特定工具或现有工具（如crudini、Git、jq）来简化处理过程。IshKebab的观点则质疑使用复杂脚本的必要性。

data.title: Photo calorie app Cal AI was built by two teenagers
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 18岁的高中生Zach Yadegari和他的合伙人Henry Langmack创办了Cal AI，一个通过拍摄食物照片来记录卡路里和营养成分的应用。尽管市场上已有类似应用，但Cal AI借助大型图像模型和开源食物数据库，实现了较高的准确性。该应用在八个月内获得了超过500万次下载，月收入超过200万美元。Yadegari自小学习编程，曾以10万美元出售了自己的第一个业务，并在疫情后与合伙人们搬到旧金山的一个黑客社区开发原型。尽管他在创业上取得了成功，但他计划上大学，而不是成为典型的硅谷辍学者。目前，Cal AI团队包括另一位合伙人Jake Castillo和八名全职员工，公司仍在快速发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI食物卡路里计算应用的有效性和实用性

不同观点：
• **lurkingllama的观点**：认为食物的外观可能误导卡路里估算。如果应用估算的卡路里过低，可能导致用户摄入过多，从而放弃减肥计划；如果估算过高，虽然会减重，但长期的热量赤字可能引发饮食疲劳和其他副作用，难以持续。

• **jake_morrison的观点**：提到过去考虑过类似的想法，但没有AI技术时，只能依靠人工分析，认为这样做不道德，因为可能会依赖低薪国家的人工劳动力来分析美国人的饮食。

• **krisoft的观点**：通过实际例子说明，像橄榄油这样高卡路里的成分，从视觉上很难判断其含量，这显示了应用在估算卡路里时可能面临的困难。

• **owenpalmer的观点**：认为如果食物有营养标签，则不需要此应用；如果没有标签，应用无法推断营养信息，因此总体上认为该应用不必要。

• **siva7的观点**：质疑该应用是否只是将OpenAI的提示包装成一个应用。

• **improbableinf的观点**：将该应用与全自动驾驶汽车类比，认为两者在准确性上都存在较大不确定性，现实中的准确性更像是虚构。

• **cedws的观点**：个人经历分享，提到在办公室工作的经历并表达对青春的反思，虽然与应用本身关系不大，但反映了对成长和工作的某种态度。

• **lysecret的观点**：认为卡路里追踪的准确性并不重要，只要用户意识到自己的饮食并进行思考，就能帮助减重。坚持才是难点。

• **Beijinger的观点**：提出另一个针对有医疗问题人群的饮食记录应用的想法，通过AI分析症状与食物的关联，解决个人健康问题。

• **hhh的观点**：认为该应用不如MyFitnessPal，且存在误导性，指出其可能盲目遵循用户输入。

• **nomilk的观点**：提到该应用创始人的大学申请被拒，尽管其有明显才华，暗示即使有才华也未必能保证成功。

• **terhechte的观点**：分享了一个类似应用的例子，虽然技术不错但未获成功，认为这与时机或运气有关。

• **jashmatthews的观点**：技术上认为应用不切实际，90%的准确性不足以支持卡路里计算，认为从图片判断卡路里是不可能的。

• **acchow的观点**：强烈怀疑应用的90%准确性，认为其只是对用户显得“貌似合理”，并批评当前许多应用通过加上“AI”标签来实现市场化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于应用的准确性和实用性，部分人认为即使不准确也能帮助用户改善饮食习惯，而另一些人则认为 inaccurate 的信息可能导致用户沮丧或误导。
• 部分讨论涉及到道德和伦理问题，例如依赖低薪劳动力进行食物分析是否合适。
• 成功与运气的关系也被提及，反映出技术产品成功背后可能存在的其他因素。

43563580.article_content:
In a world filled with “vibe coding,” Zach Yadegari, teen founder of Cal AI, stands in ironic, old-fashioned contrast.
Ironic because Yadegari and his co-founder,
H
enry Langmack
, are both just 18 years old and still in high school. Yet their story, so far, is a classic.
Launched in May, Cal AI has generated over 5 million downloads in eight months, Yadegari says. Better still, he tells TechCrunch that the customer retention rate is over 30% and that the app generated over $2 million in revenue last month.
Although TechCrunch couldn’t validate his download and revenue claims, Cal AI does have a 4.8-star rating on the Apple App Store, with 66,000 reviews, and over 1 million downloads on Google Play with a 4.8-star rating on nearly 75,000 reviews.
The concept is simple: Take a picture of the food you are about to consume, and let the app log calories and macros for you.
It’s not a unique idea. For instance, the big dog in calorie counting, MyFitnessPal, has its Meal Scan feature. Then there are apps like SnapCalorie, which was
released in 2023 and created by the founder of Google Lens.
Cal AI’s advantage, perhaps, is that it was built wholly in the age of large image models. It uses models from Anthropic and OpenAI and RAG to improve accuracy and is trained on open source food calorie and image databases from sites like GitHub.
“We have found that different models are better with different foods,” Yadegari tells TechCrunch.
Along the way, the founders coded through technical problems like recognizing ingredients from food packages or in jumbled bowls.
The result is an app that the creators say is 90% accurate, which appears to be good enough for many dieters.
Cal AI founding team:
Jake Castillo (bottom right); Blake Anderson (top right); Henry Langmack (top left); Zach Yadegari (bottom left)
Image Credits:
Cal AI
Teen coders and a hacker house
Yadegari is also earning some fame for his early success. But, unlike teen coders growing up with AI copilots, he was mastering Python and C# in middle school, he said.
Yadegari built his first business in the ninth grade and
sold it
for $100,000 to another game company, FreezeNova, when he was 16, he tells TechCrunch. “After quarantine, schools gave out Chromebooks to all of their students, and unsurprisingly, kids tried to abuse this by playing games in school,” he said.
The school responded by blocking web access to those game sites. So he “saw an opportunity” to build a website that gave access to all unblocked games.
The best part? He called the website “Totally Science” so the school wouldn’t block it, too.
With that sale, he and Langmack watched Y Combinator videos and socialized with the coder crowd on X looking for a new idea. He met Blake Anderson on X, who also became a Cal AI co-founder. Anderson, now 24, had
earned notice as a young consumer app coder
, too, for creating ChatGPT dating advice apps like RizzGPT and Umax.
Yadegari and Anderson had their idea after Yadegari began hitting the gym to gain weight and “impress girls,” he said, smiling.
Then they made another cliché choice: They moved to San Francisco to live in a hacker house while building their prototype.
But while there, Yadegari, the son of two lawyers, learned a contrarian lesson. He discovered he wanted to go to college and not become a classic Silicon Valley dropout type.
“Twenty-four-seven grinding, sleeping on the floor, actually, one of the nights, and it was a very fun time, and it taught me a lot,” he said of the experience.
But he looked around. “We were surrounded by people that were in their late 20s or 30s all day. And I realized that if I didn’t go to college, this is what life would be like.”
While he hasn’t yet determined which university he’ll attend, he and Langmack are still having fun running their company. It now includes another co-founder, Jake Castillo, 28 who is COO and running influencer marketing, as well as eight full-time employees between developers, a designer, and social media managers.
Correction: This story was updated to note that the founders are still in high school.

data.title: New antibiotic that kills drug-resistant bacteria found in technician's garden
data.author: ascorbic
data.article_summary: 研究人员在一位实验室技术员家的花园土壤中发现了一种新型抗生素分子，由**Paenibacillus**细菌产生。这种分子对包括抗药性菌株在内的多种病原菌（如**大肠杆菌**）具有强大的抗菌活性，且对人体细胞无毒。该分子通过攻击细菌的核糖体来抑制其蛋白质合成，而细菌对 targeting 核糖体的药物较难产生抗性。由于全球抗菌药物耐药性问题日益严重，每年导致大量死亡，这一发现为应对抗生素危机提供了新希望。研究成果发表于《Nature》期刊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新抗生素的发现、开发和应用中的多方面问题，包括科学、经济、政治和实际应用的挑战。

不同观点：
• mentalgear：强调抗生素在畜牧业中的滥用是抗菌素耐药性（AMR）问题的主要驱动因素，主张严格禁止在动物食品行业使用新型抗生素，并批评现代食品工业的残酷性。
• logifail：通过分享个人经历和历史案例（如从复活节岛土壤中发现雷帕霉素），指出从自然界寻找新型抗生素的潜力。
• kylehotchkiss：指出抗生素耐药性不仅是科学问题，也是政治问题。如果新型抗生素的配方未经控制就流入发展中国家，可能会导致新的耐药性问题。
• noduerme：提出通过在蘑菇或培养皿中喷洒抗药性细菌来发现新型抗生素的简单实验方法，尽管这种方法可能过于简单化。

补充讨论：
• 新抗生素的发现过程复杂且充满挑战，包括科学研究和商业化风险（yawnxyz, KSteffensen）。
• 抗生素耐药性问题不仅仅是科学问题，还涉及政治和经济因素（kylehotchkiss, KSteffensen）。
• 新型抗生素的实际应用效果和广泛性受到质疑，尤其是针对特定细菌的有效性（jakedata, pfdietz）。

• 细菌间的抗性基因转移和抗生素的滥用是抗药性问题的重要因素（djmips, pfdietz）。

• 新型抗生素的开发是否应优先考虑其商业可行性（KSteffensen的观点与其他强调科学突破的观点之间的争议）。

43538853.article_content:
New antibiotic that kills drug-resistant bacteria discovered in technician’s garden
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
You have full access to this article via your institution.
Download PDF
A species of
Paenibacillus
bacteria has potent antibacterial activity against some pathogenic bacteria such as
Escherichia coli
.
Credit: Clouds Hill Imaging Ltd/Science Photo Library
Researchers have discovered a new antibiotic molecule that targets a broad range of disease-causing bacteria — even strains resistant to commercial drugs — and is not toxic to human cells
1
.
The molecule was found in soil samples collected from a laboratory technician’s garden. The discovery shows that “there is terrifically interesting stuff hiding in plain sight”, says Kim Lewis, a microbiologist at Northeastern University in Boston, Massachusetts, who was not involved in the research. “Kudos to them that they knew what to look for.”
Podcast: New lasso-shaped antibiotic kills drug-resistant bacteria
The latest molecule targets bacteria’s protein-making factory, the ribosome, in a way that other antibiotic drugs don’t. The ribosome is an attractive antibiotic target because bacteria don’t easily develop resistance to drugs targeting the structure, adds Lewis.
The
search for new antibiotics
is necessary because bacteria acquire
resistance
to existing drugs with continued use. In 2021, bacterial resistance to antimicrobial drugs was associated with
1.1 million deaths globally
, a figure that could increase to 1.9 million by 2050.
“The antibiotic-resistance crisis is an existential threat to medicine,” says Gerry Wright, a chemical biologist at McMaster University in Hamilton, Canada, and a co-author of the study, which is published in
Nature
today.
Garden-variety bacteria
Wright and his colleagues set out to find microbes that have developed previously unknown tricks to kill pathogens. They collected soil samples in Petri dishes with growth medium and stored them for a year. The researchers then exposed the microbes from these samples to
Escherichia coli
, a common gut bacterium that can cause serious disease.
One sample showed potent antibacterial activity — by a species belonging to the genus
Paenibacillus
.
Expert take: Lasso-shaped molecule is a new type of broad-spectrum antibiotic
Further rounds of screening, genome sequencing and structural analysis revealed that the bacterium produces a molecule that belongs to a group of peptides that form a lasso-shaped knot. These peptides are known for being robust and can probably even survive being digested. “It’s a nice, really compact and incredibly robust structure,” says Wright.

data.article_summary:
**本地优先网页开发简介**

本地优先网页开发是一种让用户掌控数据的创新方法，允许用户在离线状态下使用网页应用，并在重新联网时自动同步数据。与传统网页应用依赖后端服务器不同，本地优先应用具有以下核心原则：

1. **即时访问**：无需等待数据加载或同步。
2. **设备独立性**：数据可在多个设备间无缝访问。
3. **网络独立性**：基本功能无需联网即可使用。
4. **轻松协作**：支持离线协作。
5. **未来可访问的数据**：数据长期可访问和使用。
6. **内置安全性**：设计上考虑安全和隐私。
7. **用户控制**：用户完全拥有和控制数据。

与云软件相比，本地优先软件在离线支持和数据所有权方面具有明显优势，适合文件编辑和生产力工具类应用。然而，对于需要管理现实世界资源（如银行、电商和物流）的应用，云或服务器集中模式更合适。

开发同步功能的本地优先应用面临数据冲突等挑战，需要专门的算法和数据结构来解决。

**总结**：本地优先开发强调用户数据控制和离线功能，是网页应用开发的革命性方法。

What is Local-first Web Development?
Updated:
Nov 28, 2024
at
Imagine having complete control over your data in every web app, from social media platforms to productivity tools. Picture using these apps offline with automatic synchronization when you’re back online. This is the essence of local-first web development – a revolutionary approach that puts users in control of their digital experience.
As browsers and devices become more powerful, we can now create web applications that minimize backend dependencies, eliminate loading delays, and overcome network errors. In this comprehensive guide, we’ll dive into the fundamentals of local-first web development and explore its numerous benefits for users and developers alike.
The Limitations of Traditional Web Applications
Traditional web applications rely heavily on backend servers for most operations. This dependency often results in:
Frequent loading spinners during data saves
Potential errors when the backend is unavailable
Limited or no functionality when offline
Data storage primarily in the cloud, reducing user ownership
While modern frameworks like Nuxt have improved initial load times through server-side rendering, many apps still suffer from performance issues post-load. Moreover, users often face challenges in accessing or exporting their data if an app shuts down.
Core Principles of Local-First Development
Local-first development shares similarities with offline-first approaches but goes further in prioritizing user control and data ownership. Here are the key principles that define a true local-first web application:
Instant Access:
Users can immediately access their work without waiting for data to load or sync.
Device Independence:
Data is accessible across multiple devices seamlessly.
Network Independence:
Basic tasks function without an internet connection.
Effortless Collaboration:
The app supports easy collaboration, even in offline scenarios.
Future-Proof Data:
User data remains accessible and usable over time, regardless of software changes.
Built-In Security:
Security and privacy are fundamental design considerations.
User Control:
Users have full ownership and control over their data.
It’s important to note that some features, such as account deletion, may still require real-time backend communication to maintain data integrity.
For a deeper dive into local-first software principles, check out
Ink & Switch: Seven Ideals for Local-First Software
.
Cloud vs Local-First Software Comparison
Feature
Cloud Software 🌥️
Local-First Software 💻
Real-time Collaboration
😟 Hard to implement
😊 Built for real-time sync
Offline Support
😟 Does not work offline
😊 Works offline
Service Reliability
😟 Service shuts down? Lose everything!
😊 Users can continue using local copy of software + data
Service Implementation
😟 Custom service for each app (infra, ops, on-call rotation, …)
😊 Sync service is generic → outsource to cloud vendor
Local-First Software Fit Guide
✅ Good Fit
File Editing
📝 - text editors, word processors, spreadsheets, slides, graphics, video, music, CAD, Jupyter notebooks
Productivity
📋 - notes, tasks, issues, calendar, time tracking, messaging, bookkeeping
Summary
: Ideal for apps where users freely manipulate their data
❌ Bad Fit
Money
💰 - banking, payments, ad tracking
Physical Resources
📦 - e-commerce, inventory
Vehicles
🚗 - car sharing, freight, logistics
Summary
: Better with centralized cloud/server model for real-world resource management
Types of Local-First Applications
Local-first applications can be categorized into two main types:
1. Local-Only Applications
While often mistakenly categorized as local-first, these are actually offline-first applications. They store data exclusively on the user’s device without cloud synchronization, and data transfer between devices requires manual export and import processes. This approach, while simpler to implement, doesn’t fulfill the core local-first principles of device independence and effortless collaboration. It’s more accurately described as an offline-first architecture.
2. Sync-Enabled Applications
These applications automatically synchronize user data with a cloud database, enhancing the user experience but introducing additional complexity for developers.
Challenges in Implementing Sync-Enabled Local-First Apps
Developing sync-enabled local-first applications presents unique challenges, particularly in managing data conflicts. For example, in a collaborative note-taking app, offline edits by multiple users can lead to merge conflicts upon synchronization. Resolving these conflicts requires specialized algorithms and data structures, which we’ll explore in future posts in this series.
Even for single-user applications, synchronizing local data with cloud storage demands careful consideration and additional logic.
Building Local-First Web Apps: A Step-by-Step Approach

data.article_summary: Wikimedia基金会宣布，人工智能（AI）公司的大规模数据抓取正给维基百科服务器带来沉重负担。自2024年初以来，自动化机器人通过爬虫、API和批量下载获取数据，导致带宽使用量增加了50%。这些机器人主要抓取不常访问的页面，使得缓存系统失效，增加了技术与财务成本。尽管机器人仅占总浏览量的35%，却占据了65%的最昂贵请求。许多机器人不遵守规则，伪装成人类用户，迫使平台采取防御措施。基金会正通过“WE5: 负责任的基础设施使用”计划寻找解决方案，以平衡开放性与可持续性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对大语言模型（LLMs）及其资源使用的批评与技术实现的争议

不同观点：
• [botanical] 认为当前大量资源被用于开发 barely useful 的LLMs，这些系统只是模仿人类语言，并没有真正的智能。他质疑这些技术是否能代表通用人工智能（AGI）的未来，并认为AI行业的一些表现是为了支撑其股票价格。
• [scinadier] 质疑公司为何不直接下载Wikipedia数据库，而是采取其他复杂方式，指出有更直接的数据获取途径。
• [viraptor] 不明白为什么大公司不雇佣专家进行有效的数据索引，而是进行低效的抓取，甚至冒着失去数据访问的风险。他认为可能是因为贪婪和风投资金的推动。
• [ricardobeat] 提出既然有完整的Wikipedia数据可以通过torrent获取，为何还需要去抓取Wikipedia，暗示抓取行为不必要。
• [kubb] 认为像Wikipedia这样的资源未来可能会消失，表达了对信息丢失的担忧，称之为新的黑暗时代。

补充讨论：
• [philipwhiuk] 引用了Wikipedia的OKRs，指出Wikipedia计划通过短视频内容吸引年轻人，暗示其战略转变，可能导致对传统数据获取方式的忽视。
• [gnabgib] 提到讨论链接，但没有直接表达立场，可能是在引导读者查看其他相关讨论。
• [lxgr] 也提到讨论链接，类似于[gnabgib]，没有明确表达个人观点，而是提供更多讨论背景。

争议焦点：
1. 大语言模型的实际效用和资源消耗的合理性。
2. 公司为何不采用更直接有效的方式获取数据，而是进行复杂的抓取。
3. Wikipedia战略转变和未来信息保存的问题。

这些观点反映了技术实现、资源利用和社会影响的复杂讨论。

On Tuesday, the Wikimedia Foundation
announced
that relentless AI scraping is putting strain on Wikipedia's servers. Automated bots seeking AI model training data for LLMs have been vacuuming up terabytes of data, growing the foundation's bandwidth used for downloading multimedia content by 50 percent since January 2024. It’s a scenario familiar across the free and open source software (FOSS) community, as we've
previously detailed
.
The Foundation hosts not only Wikipedia but also platforms like
Wikimedia Commons
, which offers 144 million media files under open licenses. For decades, this content has powered everything from search results to school projects. But since early 2024, AI companies have dramatically increased automated scraping through direct crawling, APIs, and bulk downloads to feed their hungry AI models. This exponential growth in non-human traffic has imposed steep technical and financial costs—often without the attribution that helps sustain Wikimedia’s volunteer ecosystem.
The impact isn’t theoretical. The foundation says that when former US President Jimmy Carter died in December 2024, his Wikipedia page predictably drew millions of views. But the real stress came when users simultaneously streamed a 1.5-hour video of a 1980 debate from Wikimedia Commons. The surge doubled Wikimedia’s normal network traffic, temporarily maxing out several of its Internet connections. Wikimedia engineers quickly rerouted traffic to reduce congestion, but the event revealed a deeper problem: The baseline bandwidth had already been consumed largely by bots scraping media at scale.
This behavior is increasingly familiar across the FOSS world. Fedora’s Pagure repository blocked all traffic from Brazil after similar scraping incidents covered by Ars Technica. GNOME’s GitLab instance implemented proof-of-work challenges to filter excessive bot access. Read the Docs dramatically cut its bandwidth costs after blocking AI crawlers.
Wikimedia’s internal data explains why this kind of traffic is so costly for open projects. Unlike humans, who tend to view popular and frequently cached articles, bots crawl obscure and less-accessed pages, forcing Wikimedia’s core datacenters to serve them directly. Caching systems designed for predictable, human browsing behavior don’t work when bots are reading the entire archive indiscriminately.
As a result, Wikimedia found that bots account for 65 percent of the most expensive requests to its core infrastructure despite making up just 35 percent of total pageviews. This asymmetry is a key technical insight: The cost of a bot request is far higher than a human one, and it adds up fast.
Crawlers that evade detection
Making the situation more difficult, many AI-focused crawlers do not play by established rules. Some ignore robots.txt directives. Others spoof browser user agents to disguise themselves as human visitors. Some even rotate through residential IP addresses to avoid blocking, tactics that have become common enough to force individual developers like Xe Iaso to adopt drastic protective measures for their code repositories.
This leaves Wikimedia’s
Site Reliability team
in a perpetual state of defense. Every hour spent rate-limiting bots or mitigating traffic surges is time not spent supporting Wikimedia’s contributors, users, or technical improvements. And it’s not just content platforms under strain. Developer infrastructure, like Wikimedia’s code review tools and bug trackers, is also frequently hit by scrapers, further diverting attention and resources.
These problems mirror others in the AI scraping ecosystem over time. Curl developer Daniel Stenberg has
previously detailed
how fake, AI-generated bug reports are wasting human time. On his blog, SourceHut’s Drew DeVault
highlight
how bots hammer endpoints like git logs, far beyond what human developers would ever need.
Across the Internet, open platforms are experimenting with technical solutions: proof-of-work challenges, slow-response tarpits (like
Nepenthes
), collaborative crawler blocklists (like "
ai.robots.txt
"), and commercial tools like Cloudflare's
AI Labyrinth
. These approaches address the technical mismatch between infrastructure designed for human readers and the industrial-scale demands of AI training.
Open commons at risk
Wikimedia acknowledges the importance of providing "knowledge as a service," and its content is indeed freely licensed. But as the Foundation states plainly, "Our content is free, our infrastructure is not."
The organization is now focusing on systemic approaches to this issue under a new initiative:
WE5: Responsible Use of Infrastructure
. It raises critical questions about guiding developers toward less resource-intensive access methods and establishing sustainable boundaries while preserving openness.
The challenge lies in bridging two worlds:

data.title: Why do we need modules at all? (2011)
data.author: matthews2
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了是否需要在编程语言中使用模块，提出了一种不同的编程方式。作者Joe Armstrong建议取消模块，所有函数拥有唯一名称和丰富的元数据，并存储在一个全局的可搜索键值数据库中。这种方式的优点包括简化代码贡献，只需添加单个函数，而不是完整的项目，同时内容经过同行评审。作者还提到当前模块系统的优缺点，例如模块提供了编译和代码分发的单元，但决定函数归属模块常常很困难，且可能破坏封装。他以Erlang中的`lists.erl`和`string.erl`为例，说明在多个模块中选择合适的一个放置函数的困惑，并介绍了自己在`elib1_misc.erl`中积累的常用函数。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于是否需要模块和层次命名空间的争论

不同观点：
• **支持模块和层次命名空间**：
  - **ludston**：认为模块有助于避免搜索结果被无关代码污染，帮助组织核心功能，避免过长的函数名前缀，如匈牙利命名法。
  - **bionhoward**：模块限制了开发者在同一时间需要处理的复杂性，符合人类记忆限制（7±2概念）。
  - **layer8**：模块不仅能将协同工作的函数组合在一起，还能隐藏实现细节（私有函数），并作为版本控制的基本单位。

• **支持扁平命名空间**：
  - **Joe**：Erlang社区成员，支持扁平命名空间，认为层次命名没有逻辑性且不扩展，用例子（啤酒和薯条）说明扁平命名足够。
  - **jasode**：指出即使没有模块，大型代码库中会通过元数据标签等方式重新发明层次结构，但扁平命名迫使函数名唯一，可能导致名称过长。

• **中立或反思性观点**：
  - **jonnycat**：虽然不完全同意反对层次命名空间的观点，但尊重提出者的专业知识，倾向于倾听和学习。
  - **andrewcl**：认为设想无模块的世界有其价值，但难以实际实现，模块作为分隔手段有其必要性。

补充讨论：
• **Unison语言的提及**：
  - **anonzzzies**和**neongreen**：提到Unison语言使用函数数据库和自由重命名标识符，可能解决部分命名空间问题。

• **对扁平命名空间的批评**：
  - **Etheryte**：质疑扁平命名空间只是将复杂性转移，而非解决，在海量函数中寻找特定函数变得困难。
  - **immibis**：通过JavaScript的npm生态系统例子，说明单一扁平命名空间会导致混乱和管理问题。

• **安全性和动态加载**：
  - **friendzis**：提出全局命名空间可能导致安全问题，特别是在动态加载代码时，模块有助于限制变更的影响范围。

• **对高级功能的设想**：
  - **wruza**：认为函数多分类、搜索等高级功能过于理想化，现实中实现难度大。

争议的焦点：模块和层次命名空间是否必要，扁平命名空间是否能有效管理大型代码库的复杂性。

Why do we need modules at all?
This is a brain-dump-stream-of-consciousness-thing. I've been
thinking about this for a while.
I'm proposing a slightly different way of programming here
The basic idea is
- do away with modules
- all functions have unique distinct names
- all functions have (lots of) meta data
- all functions go into a global (searchable) Key-value database
- we need letrec
- contribution to open source can be as simple as
contributing a single function
- there are no "open source projects" - only "the open source
Key-Value database of all functions"
- Content is peer reviewed
These are discussed in no particular order below:
Why does Erlang have modules?
There's a good an bad side to modules:
Good: Provides a unit of compilation, a unit of code
distribution. unit of code replacement
Bad: It's very difficult to decide which module to put an individual
function in. Break encapsulation (see later)
Aside: lib_misc.erl
When I'm programming I often get to the point were I say there should
a function foo/2 in lists.erl but their isn't. There should be but
there isn't - foo/2 is a small self contained thing. Why should it be
in lists.erl because it "feels right".
Strings are lists, so why do we have two modules lists.erl and
string.erl how should I decide in which module my new string/list
processing function should go.
To avoid all mental anguish when I need a small function that
should be somewhere else and isn't I stick it in
a module elib1_misc.erl.

data.title: Show HN: Transputer emulator in JavaScript (fast enough to be useful)
data.author: nanochess
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者使用Javascript实现的一个Transputer处理器模拟器。该模拟器最初是用C语言编写的，并为适应Javascript做了一些调整，如处理32位无符号整数和使用Uint8Array提高性能和内存效率。模拟器预装了作者1996年开发的操作系统，支持多驱动器和C编译器（K&R语法），并提供了一些示例命令和程序编译方法。此外，模拟器还支持运行3D建模和光线追踪程序，并展示了多任务处理的简单例子。文章最后提供了源代码链接，并邀请读者支持其创作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Transputer相关技术成就及其背景、项目独特性以及JavaScript性能问题

不同观点：

About me
Transputer emulator in Javascript
This is a Javascript port of my
transputer emulator written originally in C
for my series of articles about the transputer processor. In the old times, Javascript was an interpreted language, but since many years ago it is implemented as a JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler, so it can approach speeds closer to the C language.
Other implementation caveat here is that Javascript treats bitwise operators as generating 32-bit signed integers. This was avoided using the
>>> 0
operator (logical right-shift) because it generates a 32-bit
unsigned
integer. You can try
0x80000000 >> 0
and see how it gives back a negative number, while
0x80000000 >>> 0
preserves the unsigned value.
Another "new" thing in Javascript is
Uint8Array
, it is way faster than a normal array and
saves
memory, as there are several of these arrays (including one of 40MB to hold the entire hard disk drive!). For the drive images, I tried using an initialized array but the source code used 20 megabytes for a binary of 3 megabytes. I figured a good trick to reduce the Javascript source code size using
Base64 in my bin2.c utility
to encode the 3MB of data for the hard disk drive, and
window.atob
gets a decoded string that is copied directly to the hard disk drive's Uint8Array.
I didn't expected to have a floating-point emulation, but I discovered the
Float32Array
and Float64Array types (added in 2010) and how these can be shadowed with an Uint32Array, so the emulator can work with real floating-point math, and uses the Uint32Array to get the floating-point binary data to replicate in the transputer internal memory.
Finally, for the display I was pretty fortunate to find
jsTerm by Peter Nitsch
with a compatible license. I removed the Telnet and sockets portion. And as it used a bitmap for the font, I was able to replace it with my original font from 1996 and use it, so you can see the single-line borders for the text windows, and other special characters. My font was based on ECMA-94 (charset 1), also known as ISO-8859-1, with the $00-$1f and $80-$9f characters filled with graphics. It is based on a VGA BIOS font, and I think I improved some letters, but I don't remember which ones. Try running the
C:Conjunto
command to see all the letters and symbols.
You can give a look to the Javascript source code for this emulator at
https://github.com/nanochess/transputer/tree/master/js
What do we have here?
This emulator doesn't have options to run
my early Pascal compiler
or the
Small-C compiler
, instead it comes preloaded with
my full-blown operating system
(Spring 1996), it includes a lot of features like multiple drives (A: is a 1.44mb floppy, B: is a 512K RAM disk, C: is a 40 MB hard drive, D: is a CD-ROM in ISO-9660 format but no image can be loaded).
The C compiler supports the full K&R syntax (except for
static
and
extern
, because there's no linker).
Some commands you can test inside the operating system:
DIR A:
DIR C:
AYUDA
MEM
C:EDITOR
Use F1 (or Fn+F1 in macOS) to access the help box of the visual text editor, and type F4 (or Fn+F4 in macOS) to open the directory browsing for reading text files.
Use
C:CC
to invoke the C compiler,
C:ENS
to invoke the assembler,
C:EJECUTABLE
to build assembler output into a working executable. There are instructions for compiling programs in the
C:/Documentos/Programas.doc
file (you could try self-compiling the C compiler!)
This is an example compilation of a program:
C:CC
N
N
C:/C/Hora.c
B:Hora.len
C:ENS
B:Hora.len
C:/Lib/stdio.len
[empty line]
B:Hora.e
C:EJECUTABLE
B:Hora.e
512
0
C:Hora.p
My emulator in C is way faster than this demo, but if you have a speedy computer and a good browser, this Javascript version can be very interesting.
3D modeler
You can run the 3D modeler using this:
c:modela
c:dibujo_3d/escena_tetera
Select a mode, press Enter, and then press Enter again to start displaying. There are more scenes in the
C:/Dibujo_3D
directory, each one starts with the name
escena_
. You can list the scenes using this command:
dir c:/dibujo_3d/escena*
Ray tracer
You can run the Ray Tracer using this:
c:m3d
c:dibujo_3d/prueba
Only two M3D files are available in the
C:/Dibujo_3D
directory. You should enter the names without the extension.
Multitasking
There is a small example of multitasking, you can have a clock at the top-right of the screen. Type this command:
@c:/Desarrollo/Reloj
Source code
The source code is released at
https://github.com/nanochess/transputer

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Numbers应用的看法和使用体验，以及与Excel等其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• **支持Numbers，认为其适合轻量使用**：robin_reala认为Numbers在进行快速CSV数据操作时非常方便，不需要专门写脚本，适合轻量使用。mritchie712则用Numbers作为待办事项列表管理工具，已经使用了十年，认为其功能足够满足个人需求。

• **质疑Numbers的适用范围和支持文档**：friendzis指出Apple支持页面不够具体，无法从支持文章中明确Numbers的适用范围。这反映出用户对官方文档不够详细的困惑。

• **Numbers在深度商业需求上的不足**：MobileVet认为Numbers虽然在视觉上很美观，但在深度商业需求上仍无法与Excel相比，导致其公司不得不购买Windows设备以满足会计需求。这说明Numbers在高端商业应用中仍有很大提升空间。

• **对Numbers的陌生或无法访问**：ZeroCool2u表示从未见过Numbers的样子，因为公司MacBook上一直被硬性屏蔽。这反映了部分用户因企业政策限制而无法使用Numbers的情况。

• **对特定功能的期待和比较**：asplake询问Numbers是否具备SPLIT和JOIN功能，这是Excel中长期缺乏的功能。praestigiare则指出Numbers在共享和协作上的不便，因为大多数人都使用Excel和Google Sheets，但他承认Numbers在处理CSV和其他文本数据时表现出色。

补充讨论：
• **对标题的误解**：username135对标题产生了误解，以为讨论的是MAC地址，这显示出不同技术背景用户对同一话题可能产生的不同联想。

• **其他技术话题的插入**：jwhiles提到曾担心讨论的是AWS中的Lambda，而soegaard则提供了一个与Danish用户相关的bug报告链接。这些评论虽然与Numbers不完全相关，但体现了讨论的分散性和多样性。

• **功能扩展的期望**：MartinMond简短地提到Numbers缺少约束求解器，这表明部分用户希望Numbers能增加更多高级功能以满足复杂需求。

争议的焦点：
• Numbers是否足够强大以应对深度商业需求，特别是在与Excel的对比中表现出不足。MobileVet的经历显示出在高端应用中Numbers仍无法替代Excel。

总体来看，讨论围绕Numbers的优缺点展开，重点在于其轻量使用的便捷性和高端商业应用中的不足。官方支持文档的不明确性也引发了一些用户的困惑。

MAP
The MAP function maps each value in an array to a new value determined by a
LAMBDA
function and returns a new array.
MAP
(
array, array…, LAMBDA(element, calculation)
)
array:
The array to be mapped.
array…:
An additional input array.
LAMBDA:
A defined subformula.
element:
An input that defines the value you are passing through the formula.
calculation:
The formula you want the function to execute and return. This is required and must be the last argument.
Notes
You can use the
spilled range operator
“#” to reference an array created by a formula.

争议的焦点：
• Numbers是否足够强大以应对深度商业需求，特别是在与Excel的对比中表现出不足。MobileVet的经历显示出在高端应用中Numbers仍无法替代Excel。

总体来看，讨论围绕Numbers的优缺点展开，重点在于其轻量使用的便捷性和高端商业应用中的不足。官方支持文档的不明确性也引发了一些用户的困惑。

data.title: Study finds solo music listening boosts social well-being
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 一项由布法罗大学研究人员发表的研究表明，独自听音乐可以提升社交幸福感。该研究发表在《Psychology of Music》期刊上，指出音乐可以作为一种社交替代品，帮助人们减轻孤独感、隔离感以及应对社交威胁（如拒绝）。研究通过两个实验发现，听自己喜欢的音乐能让人感觉不那么孤独，并且在面对社交威胁时，听 favorite 音乐的人比不听的人感受到更多归属感。音乐通过让人与艺术家产生联系、沉浸于音乐世界以及唤起他人记忆等方式发挥作用。这项研究揭示了日常活动如何帮助我们保持健康和快乐。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：音乐作为背景音对个体心理和情感的影响，以及对相关研究的看法

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun认为外部音乐（通过扬声器播放）能帮助他避免脑海中的单曲循环，并且他有自己精心策划的本地播放列表，同时在实验室内则会播放新音乐进行筛选。
• tananan指出，用一种愉悦的事物替代另一种缺失的愉悦，可以帮助缓解痛苦，强调了个人喜好对享受的影响。
• singularity2001从进化角度解释音乐与群体安全感的关系，认为现代通过互联网仍能保持这种联系，但现代生活中的积极感受可能被夸大。
• SteelByte对音乐的社会效应和神经机制表示兴趣，并提到音乐疗法可能的应用前景。
• stronglikedan建议通过相对便宜的方式（如入耳式耳机）体验高保真音乐，认为这是一个既具教育意义又可能变得昂贵的爱好。
• riyanapatel分享了自己将电视节目作为背景音的独特习惯，类似于白噪音的效果。
• hk1337则提出了电视节目背景音与音乐背景音的相似性问题，认为音乐可能对某些人过于刺激。
• pearlsontheroad考虑了音乐背景音对环境自主性和控制感的潜在影响。
• ssttoo对文章标题感到困惑，期望了解独奏音乐（如单钢琴作品）的特殊性。
• ThinkBeat对研究结果表示不屑，认为其显而易见，并质疑研究对“改善”的持续时间缺乏探讨。
• euvitudo提到自己的宠物鸟在音乐播放时显得更快乐，并似乎对音乐有偏好。
• qoez讽刺地评论了人们依赖研究来获取常识的现象。
• dimal对这类研究表示厌倦，质疑其学术价值，并对科学出版的现状表示失望。
• _fat_santa则从个人经验出发，强调音乐在早晨例行活动中的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于研究的价值和创新性，部分评论者（如dimal和ThinkBeat）认为这类研究显而易见且缺乏实际意义，而其他人（如SteelByte）则对其潜在应用表示兴趣。
• 不同个体对背景音的偏好各异，如JKCalhoun偏好音乐，riyanapatel和hk1337则更喜欢电视节目作为背景音。
• 音乐对情感的正面影响被广泛认可，但具体机制和持续时间仍存在讨论空间。

Study finds solo music listening boosts social well-being
by Bert Gambini,
University at Buffalo
Credit: Unsplash/CC0 Public Domain
Listening to music by yourself might not seem like a social activity, but University at Buffalo researchers have published a study that suggests how doing so can have valuable social benefits.
"It's a great way to give yourself a social boost and increase your well-being," says Elaine Paravati, Ph.D., the study's corresponding author, who conducted the research while completing her doctorate at UB.
Across two experiments for the study
published
in the journal
Psychology of Music
, Paravati and co-authors—Esha Naidu, Ph.D., a postdoctoral associate at Duke University, who was finishing her graduate work at UB at the time of the research; and Shira Gabriel, Ph.D., a UB professor of psychology—demonstrated how music functions as a social surrogate.
The study's perspective, however, differs from a lot of previous research on the social aspects of music, which often focus on how music brings people together, as listeners and performers.
Paravati instead looked at music enjoyed in isolation.
Humans have a fundamental need to belong, which strongly motivates our behavior. Failing to connect with others can lead to depression, anxiety and low self-esteem. There are traditional ways to fill this need, like spending time with family and friends, but there are non-traditional strategies as well, activities that might not be immediately recognized as social.
These are known as social surrogates, which can buffer against loneliness, isolation and social threats, like rejection, just as well as time spent with others.
Parasocial relationships, such as the one-sided bond between fans and celebrities, immersion into the social world, and reminders of others, are all social surrogates.
"Listening to music alone operates as a social surrogate along all three of those pathways," says Paravati. "All of these paths can help us feel less lonely and more belonging. Music helps us feel connected to the artists; it can make us feel immersed in the world of music; and music can remind us of others.
"You might think you're motivated to listen to your favorite song because you think it has a catchy beat, but it's likely that you're drawn in because that music is filling your social fuel tank and helping you feel a sense of belonging."
For the study's first experiment, researchers asked participants about their use of known social surrogates, such as favorite television shows, as well as their use of music.
"We found that listening to one's favorite music helped individuals feel less lonely," says Paravati. "But someone's favorite music was more effective at this than just listening to music in general.
"In other words, there is something special about putting on your favorite song and jamming out."
For the second experiment, the researchers designed a test to measure the effectiveness of favorite music as a response to a social threat. Participants played a virtual ball-toss game often used for research on social exclusion.
"Again, those who listened to their favorite music felt more belonging than those in the control condition, suggesting that listening to their favorite music buffered against the negative effects of a social threat."
Paravati says future research might explore the impact of
music
genre or the individual differences among the three surrogate pathways and which might be more important than the other two.
"This work is another puzzle piece that shows how
little things
we do in our everyday lives help us to be as healthy and happy as possible," says Paravati.
More information:
Elaine Paravati et al, Thank you for the music: Music as a social surrogate that protects against social threats,
Psychology of Music
(2025).
DOI: 10.1177/03057356241312219

University at Buffalo

data.title: Gumroad’s source is available
data.author: philipjoubert
data.article_summary: 该文章是一个GitHub项目`antiwork/gumroad`的自述文件，主要介绍了如何设置和运行Gumroad项目的开发环境。项目使用Ruby、Node.js、Docker等技术，依赖MySQL、Percona Toolkit、ImageMagick、libvips、FFmpeg和PDFtk等工具。开发前需安装指定版本的Ruby和Node.js，并通过Docker配置开发环境。文章详细说明了各依赖工具的安装方法，以及如何通过Bundler安装Ruby gems和配置自定义凭证。此外，还提及了本地SSL证书的设置方法。项目提供了代码贡献指南、行为准则和商标指南等文件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目的价值、许可协议的合理性、项目文档的清晰度以及AI工具在项目中的潜在作用。

不同观点：
• 一些用户对项目的规模和AI工具的结合持积极态度。Multiplayer认为该项目的代码库对AI工具的改进有潜在帮助，并提到悬赏机制虽然奖金不多，但仍具激励作用。
• Shipscode对项目的许可协议表示赞赏，认为其允许创造收入，并在一定程度后才需公开代码，这比GPL的强制公开更有利，特别是对MVP开发者而言。
• 多个用户（fbn79、prakashn27、udev4096）对项目的许可协议持批评态度，认为其限制性太强，偏离了开源的本质，尤其是与MIT和GPL等传统开源许可相比。

补充讨论：
• 项目文档的清晰度受到质疑。Teekert和ErrorNoBrain指出，项目的Readme文件缺乏对项目功能的详细说明，使用户困惑。
• 一些用户对项目的实际用途和动机表示怀疑。Noname120和udev4096质疑项目的动机以及如何在许可限制下有效使用该代码。
• 关于AI工具和开源代码的结合，一些用户（如Multiplayer）表达了对AI工具如何与开源代码互补的兴趣，并探讨了悬赏和AI支出之间的关系。
• 还有用户（lionkor）以讽刺的口吻提到利用LLM模型绕过许可限制的可能性，这引发了对开源项目保护机制的进一步讨论。

争议焦点：
• 许可协议的限制性是争议的核心。部分用户认为该许可偏离了开源精神，而另一些用户则认为其提供了商业灵活性。
• 项目文档的不清晰导致用户对项目功能的理解困难，这影响了用户对项目价值的判断。

整体来看，讨论围绕项目的技术价值、许可协议的商业可行性以及文档和动机的不透明性展开。

• 关于AI工具和开源代码的结合，一些用户（如Multiplayer）表达了对AI工具如何与开源代码互补的兴趣，并探讨了悬赏和AI支出之间的关系。
• 还有用户（lionkor）以讽刺的口吻提到利用LLM模型绕过许可限制的可能性，这引发了对开源项目保护机制的进一步讨论。

• 许可协议的限制性是争议的核心。部分用户认为该许可偏离了开源精神，而另一些用户则认为其提供了商业灵活性。

data.title: On JavaScript's Weirdness
data.author: n2d4
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了JavaScript中一些鲜为人知的怪异行为，超越了常见的`'0' == 0`这类问题。作者指出了三个更隐蔽的怪癖：

1. **`eval`的特殊行为**：`eval`函数在直接调用时可以访问当前作用域，而重命名的`eval`只能访问全局作用域。这是因为ECMAScript规范对`eval`调用有特殊处理，增加了引擎的复杂性。

2. **循环变量捕获问题**：JavaScript的循环变量默认按引用捕获。在`for`循环中使用`let`定义变量时，JavaScript会进行特殊处理，使得每次循环的变量像是按值捕获，但如果在循环外定义变量则会出现不同的行为。

3. **虚假对象**：通常认为JavaScript有8个虚假值，但实际上还有一个被忽视的对象——`document.all`，它表现为虚假值但又是对象。

这些 quirks 虽然不常被提及，但在特定情况下会影响代码行为，值得开发者注意。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript（及TypeScript）中的语言特性、怪异行为及其在现代开发中的相关性

不同观点：
• pcthrowaway认为文章中对块作用域与词法作用域以及事件循环中的执行顺序存在误解。他通过示例说明`let`和`var`在循环中的不同表现，并提出解决方法（如使用IIFE）来处理变量作用域问题。
• brap引用《The Good Parts》一书，认为JavaScript确实存在一些不优雅的部分，但可以通过严格的linter和选择性忽略这些部分来使语言更加稳固和优雅。
• glenjamin对for循环行为的抱怨感到奇怪，认为当前的变量作用域设计合理，并提到Go语言也曾经历类似的语义变化。
• Leszek指出`eval`的性能成本问题，强调它对于性能优化的重要性，因为它允许解析器静态地判断变量是否可以被优化掉。
• rs186认为关于JavaScript怪异行为的讨论大多涉及过时的实践，现代开发中使用ES6+和TypeScript已经解决了这些问题，且这些怪异行为很少在生产代码中出现。
• smjburton质疑这些语言怪异行为在现代JavaScript开发中的相关性，尤其是在使用框架（如React、Vue）的情况下，这些"陷阱"在实践中并不常见。
• nobleach认为这些"怪异行为"是实际可能遇到的"陷阱"，相比"Wat视频"中的极端例子更加现实。
• vanderZwan指出+0 vs. -0的怪异行为属于浮点数特性，而非JavaScript独有问题，除非使用Math.sign或除以负零，否则对实际代码无影响。
• 0xbadcafebee对'0' == 0这种宽松比较持宽容态度，尤其是在脚本任务中，但认为不应在核心业务产品开发中使用类似Shellscript的语言。
• theThree提到TypeScript中函数参数类型不匹配导致的错误，认为这是基础知识，但可能被重复讨论。
• larrik不理解对'0' == 0的抱怨，指出HTTP和SQL中也有类似行为，并认为JavaScript和其生态系统中有更多令人烦恼的问题。
• Klaster_1认为这些怪异行为是JavaScript学习者已知的"坏部分"，重复这些基础知识无必要，文章有可能是博客垃圾重述。
• blatantly认为一些怪异行为（如for循环捕获行为、缺少分号、稀疏数组等）是可以通过linter或文档学习来避免的。
• skrebbel对`document.all`性能慢于`getElementById`感到困惑，希望了解编译器为何不直接将前者优化为后者。

补充讨论：
• 关于JavaScript怪异行为在现代开发中的实际影响存在争议，部分人认为这些陷阱在生产代码中很少遇到，尤其是在使用TypeScript和现代框架的情况下。
• 对`eval`和`document.all`等特定语言特性的性能和设计选择存在不同解释和疑惑。

data.title: Hackers strike Australia's largest pension funds in coordinated attacks
data.author: petethomas
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对数据泄露和金融诈骗事件的应对措施及责任归属

不同观点：
• IronCoder1 强调了强化安全措施的重要性，特别是对敏感财务数据而言。他认为养老基金必须优先投资于先进的网络安全防御和事件响应计划，且透明的沟通对于维护信任和减轻潜在损害至关重要。

• trollbridge 分享了他们防止发票诈骗的详细措施，包括使用专门的银行账户接受存款并立即转移资金，严格的支付信息变更程序，以及对客户的警示和建议。他们声称至今没有因诈骗损失任何资金，显示出其措施的有效性。

• seb1240 对养老金损失表示不满，认为应该是养老基金因为安全 breach 而遭受损失，而不是个人。他将此与银行被抢劫类比，认为个人不应承担责任。

• taberiand 认为，基于600个账户平均损失800美元的情况，以及假设用户密码安全不佳，事件的损失并不严重。他还指出快速检测和立即锁定的反应是有效和良好的。

• dbetteridge 批评了其超级基金在多因素认证（MFA）选项上仅提供短信或电子邮件的方式，暗示这种安全性不足可能是导致安全事件的原因。

• oldandboring 提供了一个存档链接，可能指向相关事件的进一步信息或讨论。

• damhsa 将此次损失与工资盗窃、通货膨胀、租金、利息等资本扩张形式进行了对比，引用《共产党宣言》暗示这些损失在更广泛的社会经济背景下并不显著。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是责任归属问题，seb1240 认为个人不应为养老基金的安全 breach 承担损失。
• 另一个讨论点是安全措施的有效性，trollbridge 详细描述了其公司防止诈骗的措施，显示出实践中的成功案例。
• 对事件响应的评价也有分歧，IronCoder1 强调了透明沟通和快速行动的重要性，而 taberiand 则认为基于事件的规模，现有的应对已经足够有效。
• dbetteridge 对认证方式的批评指向了技术实现上的安全漏洞，提示了安全措施中的潜在缺陷。
• damhsa 从更广泛的社会经济学视角看待此次事件的损失，将其与更大范围的经济现象进行对比。

data.title: Doge staffer's YouTube nickname accidentally revealed his teen hacking activity
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
Christopher Stanley，一名由埃隆·马斯克的政府效率部门（DOGE）派往美国司法部（DOJ）的SpaceX和X工程师，被曝曾夸耀从事黑客活动，包括分发盗版电子书、盗版软件和游戏作弊工具。这些夸耀出现在一些网站的存档中，被举报后迅速删除。尽管马斯克声称DOGE运作透明，但其员工身份和政府角色鲜为人知。斯坦利在DOJ的具体职责不明，但其涉及的办公室负责调查包括黑客在内的网络犯罪活动。

斯坦利的可疑过去可追溯到2006年，当时他还在高中。他使用多个网名，如Reneg4d3，在不同网站和论坛上活跃。15岁时，他创建了一个包含不当内容的网站，并夸耀攻击服务器。16岁时，他通过漏洞获取管理权限，并贬低其他论坛。他还涉及创建多个黑客论坛，尽管曾因黑客活动被网络服务提供商暂停服务，但并未停止相关活动。

2010年，斯坦利声称因收到法律威胁不再从事黑客活动，但2014年又参与Lizard Squad的黑客活动。专家认为，斯坦利的黑客背景是一个危险信号，特别是如果他在处理敏感信息时。DOGE员工的身份问题也引发了更多关注和调查要求。
data.comments_summary:

• **怀旧与隐私保护的庆幸**：KillenBoek和INTPenis等人表示，庆幸自己年轻时的行为没有被互联网记录下来，能够保护个人隐私。他们认为，过去在互联网不发达的时代成长是一种幸运，因为那些愚蠢的行为不会被永久记录和公开。
• **现代匿名的便利与误解**：firefax认为，现代技术让匿名更加容易，但年轻人可能误将这种技术便利视为技能的体现，从而导致错误判断。他指出，现代的匿名手段（如星巴克热点、一次性手机卡）让隐藏身份变得简单，但并不代表技术能力提升。
• **黑客经历的价值与负面影响**：SenorKimchi和mschuster91等人认为，青少年时期的黒客行为可能在当今法律下被过度负面解读。他们指出，许多有才华的技术人员在年轻时都有过类似的探索和犯错经历，而这些经历实际上可能培养了他们的技术能力。同时，也有人（如ZeroGravitas）认为，为某些公司工作（如DOGE）可能对个人声誉影响更大。
• **历史行为不应定义个人**：moktonar和rob等人强调，不能仅凭过去的错误行为来评判一个人。他们举例说明，一些曾经有过黒客行为的人后来成为了非常优秀的技术人员。
• **对媒体报道的批评**：soulofmischief和whywhywhywhy批评媒体对青少年黒客行为的过度报道和负面解读，认为这是对正常青春期探索行为的夸大。

• **社会对黒客行为的反应**：部分评论涉及社会和法律系统如何看待和处理青少年黒客行为，以及这些行为在个人成长和职业发展中的角色。

A SpaceX and X engineer, Christopher Stanley—currently serving as a senior advisor in the Deputy Attorney General's office at the Department of Justice (DOJ)—was reportedly caught bragging about hacking and distributing pirated e-books, bootleg software, and game cheats.
The boasts appeared on archived versions of websites, of which several, once flagged, were quickly deleted, Reuters
reported
.
Stanley was assigned to the DOJ by Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). While Musk claims that DOGE operates transparently, not much is known about who the staffers are or what their government roles entail. It remains unclear what Stanley does at DOJ, but Reuters noted that the Deputy Attorney General’s office is in charge of investigations into various crimes, "including hacking and other malicious cyber activity." Declining to comment further, the DOJ did confirm that as a "special government employee," like Musk, Stanley does not draw a government salary.
The engineer's questionable past seemingly dates back to 2006, Reuters reported, when Stanley was still in high school. The news site connected Stanley to various sites and forums by tracing various pseudonyms he still uses, including Reneg4d3, a nickname he still uses on YouTube. The outlet then further verified the connection "by cross-referencing the sites’ registration data against his old email address and by matching Reneg4d3’s biographical data to Stanley’s."
Among his earliest sites was one featuring a "crude sketch of a penis" called fkn-pwnd.com, where Stanley, at 15, bragged about "fucking up servers," a now-deleted Internet Archive screenshot reportedly showed. Another, reneg4d3.com, was launched when he was 16. There, Stanley branded a competing messaging board "stupid noobs" after supposedly gaining admin access through an "easy exploit," Reuters reported. On Bluesky, an account called "doge whisperer"
alleges
even more hacking activity, some of which appears to be corroborated by an IA
screenshot
of another site Stanley created, electonic.net (sic), which as of this writing can still be accessed.
At this time, Stanley seemed unafraid of consequences. His Internet service provider once suspended him for targeting a rival game-cheating site, Reuters reported. He'd supposedly hijacked and defaced the site with a message that confirmed, "This site has been hacked by RENEG4D3.com," according to a screenshot of the rival site preserved by DomainTools. But that suspension didn't stop him from creating other hacker forums on sites like error33.net, IA's now-deleted archive reportedly showed, and electonic.net.
However, around the age of 19, Stanley appeared to understand that publicly bragging about hacking might not be the best idea. After supposedly receiving a legal threat from a South Korean gaming company Nexon Co, he claimed in a 2010 post that "I no longer hack into Paypals, gain root access into other peoples computer (sic), or exploit online websites," Reuters reported. (Nexon told Reuters it could find no information on the alleged legal threat.)
SpaceX and X so far have not commented on the report. Hours after Reuters reached out to Stanley—who did not respond to a request for comment—"several of his old websites vanished from the Internet Archive," Reuters reported. IA confirmed that "people who own the rights to sites can request to have their content withheld from the archive," but declined to answer specific questions about the removals.
Experts see hacker past as red flag
Six former DOJ officials told Reuters that Stanley's background as a hacker "raised red flags," particularly if he's handling sensitive information that, if exposed, could reveal how federal probes are conducted or violate grand jury secrecy rules.
Among them was Jonathan Rusch, a 25-year DOJ veteran prosecutor now in academia, who told Reuters that Stanley's apparent history of disclosing illegally acquired data should have prompted "serious concerns." A background check may also have flagged that after Stanley claimed to be done with hacking,  he, in 2014, "posted footage of himself carrying out a hack" for a hacking group called Lizard Squad. That year, Lizard Squad
took credit for attacks against Sony's PlayStation Network
, Reuters noted.
Stanley's past isn't the only one raising eyebrows across government, as DOGE workers' identities are slowly learned, commonly revealed through court filings and media reports.
One of the earliest known DOGE staffers, Marko Elez, resigned after racist social media posts from his past were surfaced, The Wall Street Journal
reported
. And last week, Democrats in the Republican-controlled House of Representatives Oversight Committee demanded a "full investigation into WHO is working for DOGE" after Reuters
reported
that records apparently linked another DOGE staffer, Edward Cor

Christopher Stanley，一名由埃隆·马斯克的政府效率部门（DOGE）派往美国司法部（DOJ）的SpaceX和X工程师，被曝曾夸耀从事黑客活动，包括分发盗版电子书、盗版软件和游戏作弊工具。这些夸耀出现在一些网站的存档中，被举报后迅速删除。尽管马斯克声称DOGE运作透明，但其员工身份和政府角色鲜为人知。斯坦利在DOJ的具体职责不明，但其涉及的办公室负责调查包括黑客在内的网络犯罪活动。

斯坦利的可疑过去可追溯到2006年，当时他还在高中。他使用多个网名，如Reneg4d3，在不同网站和论坛上活跃。15岁时，他创建了一个包含不当内容的网站，并夸耀攻击服务器。16岁时，他通过漏洞获取管理权限，并贬低其他论坛。他还涉及创建多个黑客论坛，尽管曾因黑客活动被网络服务提供商暂停服务，但并未停止相关活动。

2010年，斯坦利声称因收到法律威胁不再从事黑客活动，但2014年又参与Lizard Squad的黑客活动。专家认为，斯坦利的黑客背景是一个危险信号，特别是如果他在处理敏感信息时。DOGE员工的身份问题也引发了更多关注和调查要求。

data.title: DeepSeek: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
data.author: tim_sw
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了如何通过推理时扩展计算资源来改进大型语言模型（LLM）的奖励建模（RM），提出了**推理时可扩展的通用奖励建模**方法。作者采用逐点生成奖励模型（GRM）以适应不同输入类型，并提出自原理批评调优（SPCT）方法，通过在线强化学习提高GRM的可扩展性和奖励生成效果，构建了**DeepSeek-GRM**模型。实验表明，SPCT显著提升了GRM的质量和可扩展性，在多种RM基准上优于现有方法，且优于训练时扩展。模型将开源。

Title:
Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
Authors:
Zijun Liu
,

View a PDF of the paper titled Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling, by Zijun Liu and 7 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Reinforcement learning (RL) has been widely adopted in post-training for large language models (LLMs) at scale. Recently, the incentivization of reasoning capabilities in LLMs from RL indicates that $\textit{proper learning methods could enable effective inference-time scalability}$. A key challenge of RL is to obtain accurate reward signals for LLMs in various domains beyond verifiable questions or artificial rules. In this work, we investigate how to improve reward modeling (RM) with more inference compute for general queries, i.e. the $\textbf{inference-time scalability of generalist RM}$, and further, how to improve the effectiveness of performance-compute scaling with proper learning methods. For the RM approach, we adopt pointwise generative reward modeling (GRM) to enable flexibility for different input types and potential for inference-time scaling. For the learning method, we propose Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) to foster scalable reward generation behaviors in GRMs through online RL, to generate principles adaptively and critiques accurately, resulting in $\textbf{DeepSeek-GRM}$ models. Furthermore, for effective inference-time scaling, we use parallel sampling to expand compute usage, and introduce a meta RM to guide voting process for better scaling performance. Empirically, we show that SPCT significantly improves the quality and scalability of GRMs, outperforming existing methods and models in various RM benchmarks without severe biases, and could achieve better performance compared to training-time scaling. DeepSeek-GRM still meets challenges in some tasks, which we believe can be addressed by future efforts in generalist reward systems. The models will be released and open-sourced.
