Benchi
Benchi is a minimal benchmarking framework designed to help you measure the
performance of your applications and infrastructure. It leverages Docker to
create isolated environments for running benchmarks and collecting metrics.
It was developed to simplify the process of setting up and running benchmarks
for
Conduit
.
Features
Docker Integration
: Define and manage your benchmarking environments using
Docker Compose.
Metrics Collection
: Collect and export metrics in CSV format for further
analysis.
Custom Hooks
: Define custom hooks to run commands at various stages of the
benchmark.
Progress Monitoring
: Real-time monitoring of container statuses and
metrics during the benchmark run.
Installation
To install Benchi, download
the
latest release
or
install it using Go:
go install github.com/conduitio/benchi/cmd/benchi@latest
Alternatively, you can install just the Benchi binary on a Linux OS with:
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ConduitIO/benchi/main/install.sh
|
sh
Usage
Running Benchmarks
Run benchi and point
-config
to a benchmark
configuration file
.
The repository includes an
example benchmark
, which can be run
using the following command:
benchi -config ./example/bench-kafka-kafka/bench.yml
Results
Running the benchmark will store the results in a folder named after the current
date and time inside of
results
(e.g.
results/20060102_150405
). You can
adjust the output folder using the
-out
flag.
The output folder will contain two files:
benchi.log
: Log file containing the full output of benchi.
aggregated-results.csv
: Aggregated metric results from all collectors and
all tests. The results are aggregated using a
trimmed mean
, where the top
and bottom 5% of the results are removed. Benchi also disregards any 0 values
from the start and end of the test, to accomodate for warm-up and cool-down
periods.
The output folder will also contain one folder per benchmark run (i.e. per test
and tool combination). Each benchmark run folder will contain:
infra_NAME.log
: Log file containing the output of the infrastructure docker
containers, split per infra service.
tool_NAME.log
: Log file containing the output of the tool docker containers.
COLLECTOR.csv
: Raw metrics collected using the corresponding
metrics collector
.
Command-Line Flags
-config
: Path to the benchmark config file (required).
-out
: Path to the output folder (default:
./results/${now}
*).
-tool
: Filter tool to be tested (can be provided multiple times).
-tests
: Filter test to run (can be provided multiple times).
*
${now}
is replaced with the current time formatted as
YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS
.
Docker network
Benchi creates a Docker network named
benchi
to connect the infrastructure
services and tools. This network is created automatically and removed after the
benchmark run. Please make sure to connect your services to this network to
ensure they can communicate with each other.
Example Docker Compose configuration:
services
:
my-service
:
networks
:
-
benchi
networks
:
benchi
:
external
:
true
Environment variables
Benchi runs all Docker Compose commands using the same environment variables as
the current shell. This means that you can use environment variables to pass
values to your services.
For instance, having the following Docker Compose configuration:
services
:
my-service
:
environment
:
-
MY_ENV_VAR=${MY_ENV_VAR}
You can inject the environment variable by running Benchi as follows:
MY_ENV_VAR=my-value benchi -config ./my-benchmark.yml
Configuration
Benchi uses a YAML configuration file to define the benchmark in combination
with Docker Compose configurations.
Below is an example configuration:
infrastructure

database
:
compose
:
"
./compose-database.yml
"
cache
:
compose
:
"
./compose-cache.yml
"
tools

my-app

./compose-my-app.yml
"

http://localhost:9090/metrics

主要讨论点：求职者背景及技术能力

不同观点：
• **jcadam**：拥有19年经验的高级工程师，专注于Clojure、Scala、Java等技术，最近负责知识图谱平台的开发，倾向于全职或合同工，不考虑迁移。
• **Pansy3**：全栈工程师，拥有超过五年的经验，精通TypeScript、Python和Java，愿意迁移到欧洲，灵活适应远程和现场工作环境。
• **arp242**：主要使用Go语言，具有广泛的技术背景，包括Python、Ruby、JavaScript等，对具体编程语言不太在意，愿意迁移到爱尔兰。
• **thecolorblue**：高级软件工程师，专注于React、TypeScript和机器学习应用，有数据工程和全栈开发经验，对LLMs和ML有浓厚兴趣，愿意迁移。
• **brendan_bormann**：九年经验，专注于Rust和TypeScript，全栈开发经验丰富，倾向于寻找创新和文化良好的团队，不愿意迁移但可以频繁出差。

补充讨论：
• **cplanas**：拥有超过15年经验，特别擅长Ruby和Rails，曾在Zendesk担任技术领导，著有《Rails Scales!》，不愿意迁移但愿意定期访问办公室。
• **XVincentX**：十年经验，专注于Clojure和TypeScript，曾参与API工具开发，愿意在特定情况下迁移，擅长处理技术债务和大型系统架构。
• **ryanscript01123**：全栈高级开发者，拥有多种技术经验，包括Svelte、React、Go等，有NOAA项目经验，不愿意迁移但愿意接受远程或合同工作。
• **tkrulewich**：拥有ReactJS、Next.JS和LLMs经验，曾在大学研究LLMs和网络安全，愿意在特定情况下迁移。
• **tonko**：15年以上全栈开发经验，擅长NodeJS、.NET和React，不愿意迁移但适应不同时间区工作。
• **midwestFriend**：全栈开发者，拥有多种技术经验，包括TypeScript、Java、Python等，不愿意迁移。
• **gionik97**：前端开发者，拥有四年经验，擅长Wordpress和ReactJS，不愿意迁移但适应不同时间区工作。
• **nathan_douglas**：DevOps/Platform工程师，拥有广泛技术背景，正在转向MLOps和HPC，不愿意迁移但有雄心勃勃的职业目标。
• **rishabh16**：产品管理和增长营销背景，不愿意迁移但可以访问。

争议焦点：
• 迁移意愿：求职者在迁移问题上存在显著分歧，一些人愿意迁移以寻求新机会，而另一些人则因个人或职业原因不愿意迁移。
• 技术专长：求职者技术背景广泛，从高级语言开发到全栈开发，再到DevOps和ML，反映了不同的技术深度和广度。

总结：求职者们展示了多样的技术能力、工作经验和迁移意愿，雇主需要根据具体需求评估这些因素。

data.title: Show HN: OCR pipeline for ML training (tables, diagrams, math, multilingual)
data.author: ses425500000
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个多模态OCR系统，专为从复杂教育材料中提取结构化数据而设计，特别适合机器学习（ML）训练。该系统支持多语言文本、数学公式、表格、图表和图解的识别，并生成适合AI训练的JSON或Markdown格式输出，包括自然语言描述。系统具有高精度（90–95%以上），支持日语、韩语和英语，并可扩展至其他语言。它能够处理密集科学内容和复杂布局的考试风格PDF。主要技术包括DocLayout-YOLO、Google Vision API、MathPix OCR等。示例输出展示了系统在真实数学和生物学题目中的应用，包括图像描述和相关知识点的解释。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕OCR数据提取和处理 pipeline 的技术实现、应用效果以及伦理和数据权限问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **jlcases**：认为从非结构化文档中提取信息并进行语义结构化处理是当前机器学习模型训练的瓶颈。强调在OCR之后，如何将提取的数据组织成层次化的知识结构（例如MECE框架）是关键，有助于提升下游ML任务的效果。同时提出问题，询问该pipeline是否具备超出基础布局分析的语义结构化能力。

• **novaRom**：介绍了pipeline中使用的技术工具，包括DocLayout-YOLO、Google Vision API、Gemini Pro Vision、MathPix OCR、OpenAI API等，并指出整个pipeline未开源。

• **themanmaran**：关注文本语言的保留问题，强调在处理多语言文档时不应改变原始语言，并提到使用双重提示（double prompting）来防止GPT模型随机翻译文本，解决了自己以前遇到的问题。

• **GPerson**：提出伦理问题，质疑pipeline使用的数据集是否经过合法的授权用于训练。

• **sandreas**：比较了该pipeline与"marker"工具（由VikParuchuri开发的开源项目）的差异，询问其相对优势和特点。

• **liangzhe88**：表示对pipeline未来更新的兴趣，认为当前的实现很有趣，期待后续发展。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现的细节**：novaRom列举了多个技术工具，显示出该pipeline的复杂性和对多种先进技术的整合。
• **语义结构化的需求**：jlcases强调了在OCR数据处理中，从布局分析到语义结构化的进阶需求，指出了未来发展的方向。
• **伦理与权限问题**：GPerson提出的数据集授权问题引发了对该pipeline在伦理和法律层面上的关注。
• **工具比较**：sandreas提到了与"marker"工具的对比，说明社区中存在对不同OCR解决方案的性能和功能比较。

OCR System Optimized for Machine Learning: Figures, Diagrams, Tables, Math & Multilingual Text
Overview
This OCR system is specifically designed to extract structured data from complex educational materials—such as exam papers—in a format optimized for machine learning (ML) training.
It supports multilingual text, mathematical formulas, tables, diagrams, and charts, making it ideal for creating high-quality training datasets.
Key Features
– Optimized for ML Training: Extracted elements such as diagrams, tables, and figures are semantically annotated with contextual explanations.
This includes automatic generation of natural language descriptions for visual content (e.g., “This figure shows the process of mitosis in four stages”) to enhance downstream model training.
– Multilingual Support: Works with Japanese, Korean, and English, and can be easily customized for additional languages.
– Structured Output: Generates AI-ready outputs in JSON or Markdown, including human-readable descriptions of mathematical expressions, table summaries, and figure captions.
– High Accuracy: Achieves over 90–95% accuracy on real-world academic datasets such as EJU Biology and UTokyo Math.
– Complex Layout Support: Accurately processes exam-style PDFs with dense scientific content, formula-heavy paragraphs, and rich visual elements.
– Built With: DocLayout-YOLO, Google Vision API, Gemini Pro Vision, MathPix OCR, OpenAI API, OpenCV, and more.
Sample Outputs
Below are actual examples of outputs generated by this system using real-world materials (2017 EJU Biology & 2014 University of Tokyo Math), including English-translated semantic context and extracted data.

主要讨论点：围绕OCR数据提取和处理 pipeline 的技术实现、应用效果以及伦理和数据权限问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **jlcases**：认为从非结构化文档中提取信息并进行语义结构化处理是当前机器学习模型训练的瓶颈。强调在OCR之后，如何将提取的数据组织成层次化的知识结构（例如MECE框架）是关键，有助于提升下游ML任务的效果。同时提出问题，询问该pipeline是否具备超出基础布局分析的语义结构化能力。

• **novaRom**：介绍了pipeline中使用的技术工具，包括DocLayout-YOLO、Google Vision API、Gemini Pro Vision、MathPix OCR、OpenAI API等，并指出整个pipeline未开源。

• **themanmaran**：关注文本语言的保留问题，强调在处理多语言文档时不应改变原始语言，并提到使用双重提示（double prompting）来防止GPT模型随机翻译文本，解决了自己以前遇到的问题。

• **GPerson**：提出伦理问题，质疑pipeline使用的数据集是否经过合法的授权用于训练。

• **sandreas**：比较了该pipeline与"marker"工具（由VikParuchuri开发的开源项目）的差异，询问其相对优势和特点。

• **liangzhe88**：表示对pipeline未来更新的兴趣，认为当前的实现很有趣，期待后续发展。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现的细节**：novaRom列举了多个技术工具，显示出该pipeline的复杂性和对多种先进技术的整合。
• **语义结构化的需求**：jlcases强调了在OCR数据处理中，从布局分析到语义结构化的进阶需求，指出了未来发展的方向。
• **伦理与权限问题**：GPerson提出的数据集授权问题引发了对该pipeline在伦理和法律层面上的关注。
• **工具比较**：sandreas提到了与"marker"工具的对比，说明社区中存在对不同OCR解决方案的性能和功能比较。

data.title: I don't like traveling anymore
data.author: mavidser
data.article_summary: 作者在20多岁时非常热衷于旅行，享受不同地方的自然、美食、文化和人与人之间的互动。然而，在2020年疫情期间搬到印度果阿后，生活成本降低，时间变得充裕，他得以深入发展个人兴趣如绘画、音乐和运动，并与当地社区建立了深厚联系。这让他感到更加智慧、友善和快乐，也不再觉得有必要通过旅行来获得这些成长。尽管他偶尔还会旅行，但感到这些旅行缺乏灵魂，意识到自己只是一个短暂停留的游客，无法再像过去那样开阔视野。他认为现代信息的普及也让旅行体验变得不再独特，因为很多信息通过互联网也能获取。作者目前更享受在家中与人的深厚、持久的关系，而非旅行中的短暂相遇。他暂时对旅行的兴趣减弱，可能只是暂时的状态，未来可能会找到新的旅行理由。目前，他的旅行仅限于拜访朋友或参加会议和节日。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：旅行的方式和意义，包括个人与团体旅行、旅行目的、年龄对旅行态度的影响等。

不同观点：
• **团体旅行与个人旅行的历史及现状**：
  - [keiferski] 认为，过去的旅行常以团体或社会形式进行，而现代更常见的是个人旅行。现代技术与政治发展使得个人旅行成为可能，但团体旅行的开放空间已经消失，可能要等到人类探索新星球时才会重新出现。
  
• **旅行与度假的对比**：
  - [pj_mukh] 提出，年纪渐长后，更喜欢"度假"而非"旅行"。在体验过不同文化后，人们会发现大家的需求和愿望相似。相比探索"真实文化"，更享受奢华度假（如住四季度假村），但年轻时应体验更多文化。

• **旅行的意义随年龄变化**：

• **旅行倦怠与重新评估**：
  - [ggm] 认为，年纪增长使人更智慧，但有些人即使年轻也会重新评估旅行的价值。在疫情后，对重回旅行生活感到复杂，部分原因是已经体验过大量旅行。
  
• **旅行目的与方式的选择**：
  - [nofalsescotsman] 喜欢旅行，但不喜欢无目的的旅行，倾向于有具体目标的旅行（如探访祖籍或文化兴趣）。认为稳定的家庭和熟悉的人际关系同样重要。

  - [faustlast] 提到，随着时间推移，对大城市旅行的兴趣减少，更喜欢自然和小冒险。
  - [xingwu] 建议根据自己喜欢的元素选择定居地，而非不断旅行寻找相似风格的地方。

补充讨论：
• **旅行中的文化体验与挑战**：
  - [pj_mukh] 提到，通过参与高强度运动或活动（如远足、冲浪比赛）可以快速提升文化适应力，并强调购买旅行保险的重要性。

• **对旅行魅力的感受变化**：
  - [sky_rw] 以幽默方式指出，年纪渐长后，住在第三世界国家的青年旅舍不再有吸引力。

争议焦点：旅行究竟是为了探索新文化，还是为了享受舒适和度假，尤其是在不同年龄段对旅行的态度变化。

43590973.article_content:
I don't like traveling anymore
Apr 03, 2025
One of my biggest motivators to make money in my early 20s was traveling. I would book one way tickets to places near and far, enjoy the nature, the food, the culture, and the lovely people. I would come back a slightly wiser, friendlier and a happier person.
Then, in late 2020, at the age of 25, in the middle of the pandemic, I moved to
Goa, India
. It’s a popular tourist destination, known for its beaches, though I stay far away from the beach, on a lovely farm.
My rent got a lot cheaper, and my cost of living got
a lot
cheaper. What I didn’t expect was that I also had more time in life–all my friends live close to me, distances are quicker to traverse, and the low population density means that I can make easier and longer lasting connections with my favorite restaurateur, barkeepers, entertainers and neighbors. I get the pleasure to nod/wave
Hi
to ~10 people on the 3 minute walk to my local grocery store, every day.
I found the time to learn to draw, to make music, to film and edit movies, and more forms of art. I discovered how much I enjoyed refining the use of my body. I work out in various ways–climbing different terrains, rollerblading across empty streets, surfing tall waves, and playing many sports in empty and free public parks. I discovered a love for hosting friends who come to visit my town–organizing my home into a space which is optimized for myself, and easily accessible to anyone else living there.
Sometimes, I would also work a job to pay for all these bills. And so, while doing all of this, 5 odd years have passed by. I think I am a wiser, friendlier and a happier person now.
And now, I don’t feel like traveling anymore.
It’s not that I haven’t traveled since the pandemic–but most of it has been with family and friends, which is unlike how I have always traveled. I don’t really consider that as my form of traveling though, since the collaboration and negotiations involved in group trips is not very aligned with how I usually live my life–which is slow, independent, less-structured and community oriented. This also reflects a lot in my
relationships with people
.
Last year, I turned 30. Among the many reflections one usually does on such a birthday, I thought about travel, and my long-term career goals.
Maybe I should start traveling again, which would motivate me to make a lot more money.
And so I traveled. Right now, I am writing this essay from the living room of my hostel in Almaty, Kazakhstan. I am also volunteering here because I like to be useful, have people rely on me, and work with the community. I like the people I am staying with. The staff and I have become good friends. I like the city, and have met wonderful local and foreign people in buses, bars and canyons. I go snowboarding almost daily, and the guy who runs the snowboard rental shop greets me warmly every day, while he pulls my favorite boots out the back. The boots will go back into regular circulation after I’ve left town.
And yet, the travel itself feels soulless. I am acutely aware of my status as a tourist among all of these people–someone who has objectified the life of a town as a transient
experience
, after which I go back to my regular life, where I perhaps tell stories of my travels and how much fun it was to live among a different people.
Earlier, meeting people from different places expanded my worldview, and made me aware of new ways of life. Now, everyone feels almost the same, dealing with similar issues, caring about similar things. And this isn’t just about geography–across politics, gender, economics, class, people feel the same to me at their core. Just human beings, trying to make the lives of themselves and their community slightly better, though sometimes in very myopic ways.
I will soon go back to India, where I will wait out the summer in the Himalayas. I will build furniture and gardens for my new host, in exchange for food and stay, while I work on some new software/music/film project. I am looking forward to it, but I am looking forward way more to the end of summer, when I go back home, where the connection to people isn’t already punctuated by my impending departure–where every connection feels limitless, open-ended, full of possibility.
Maybe part of my blame lies with the ubiquity of information on the internet. I love going to museums and learning about the history of a place. But barely have I felt that I couldn’t have gotten this information over the internet, if it was available there in a similarly structured manner. I meet interesting people from all over during my travels, but the same people also come to Goa often, where I end up having similar conversations.
Or maybe I am just going through a rooting phase, and one day I will get over it, and find new reasons for travel. I wait patiently for them to reveal themselves. Until then my travel will be limited to visiting friends, meetups/conferences/festivals, or going to local waterfalls,

data.title: Ferron – A fast, memory-safe web server written in Rust
data.author: lamg
data.article_summary:
Ferron 是一个用 Rust 编写的高性能、内存安全的Web服务器。它具有以下特点：高性能（利用Rust的异步能力）、内存安全、可扩展性（模块化架构）和安全性（注重安全实践和并发处理）。主要组件包括：  
- **ferron**：主服务器。  
- **ferron-passwd**：用于生成用户条目和密码哈希的工具。  

目前，Ferron 仍在开发中，可通过克隆代码库并使用 Cargo 构建和运行：  
```bash  
git clone https://github.com/ferronweb/ferron.git  
cd ferron  
cargo build -r  
cargo run -r --bin ferron  
```  
服务器配置可参考 Ferron 文档。Ferron 使用 MIT 许可证，并欢迎社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Ferron web服务器及其功能、性能、安全性、TLS支持、文档问题以及与其他服务器的比较等方面展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对服务器"快速"定义的看法**：Austin-cheney认为"快速"只是流和管道的问题，与编写语言无关，强调配置简单性和低级别操作（如流和管道）。他还特别提到对TLS证书的厌恶。
• **与Caddy的比较**：DoctorOW认为Ferron可能比Caddy更具扩展性，并且配置不会过于冗长，正在考虑迁移。
• **性能比较**：Password4312提出Rust编写的静态web服务器在TechEmpower测试中表现优异，但这些服务器并非通用目的。同时提到个人使用的Dufs支持文件上传功能。
• **TLS支持的必要性**：Arnath质疑现代web服务器是否仍需内置TLS支持，认为可以在边缘终止HTTPS。
• **对Go语言的看法**：Nottorp认为Go语言是编写服务器的更好选择，具有高性能和内存安全性。

补充讨论：
• **文档问题**：Kapilvt提到文档链接返回403错误，影响使用体验。
• **缺乏Nginx的比较**：No_wizard和Bitbasher质疑为何未与Nginx进行比较，Nginx是极其流行的web服务器。
• **安全性讨论**：Timeflex对Ferron主页上通过curl命令直接导入shell脚本的方式表示安全担忧。
• **内存使用和适用场景**：Tepix关心Ferron在低内存设备（如Raspberry Pi 1）上的适用性。
• **功能需求**：Liveafterlove询问Ferron是否支持DTSL用于WebRTC，指出Nginx目前仅提供补丁支持。

争议焦点：
• **TLS支持的必要性**：Arnath认为TLS应在边缘处理，而Austin-cheney则强烈反对证书的复杂性，显示出对TLS支持的不同看法。
• **性能比较的缺失**：多个评论者提到缺乏与Nginx的直接性能对比，质疑Ferron的真实性能表现。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **迁移意愿**：DoctorOW表现出对Ferron的兴趣，正在考虑从Caddy迁移，显示出Ferron在某些用户群体中的潜在吸引力。
• **个性化推荐**：Password4312根据个人经验推荐了其他工具（如Dufs），提供了实用案例。

总体而言，讨论围绕Ferron的功能实现、性能、安全性及其与其他服务器的比较展开，用户关注点集中在配置简便性、TLS处理和实际性能表现。

- a fast, memory-safe web server written in Rust
Features
High performance
- built with Rust’s async capabilities for optimal speed.
Memory-safe
- built with Rust, which is a programming language offering memory safety.
Extensibility
- modular architecture for easy customization.
Secure
- focus on robust security practices and safe concurrency.
Components
Ferron consists of multiple components:
ferron
: The main web server.
ferron-passwd
: A tool for generating user entries with hashed passwords, which can be copied into the web server's configuration file.
Installation
Since Ferron is still a work in progress, installation instructions will be provided once an initial release is available. Stay tuned!
Building Ferron
You can clone the repository and explore the existing code:
git clone https://github.com/ferronweb/ferron.git
cd
ferron
You can then build and run the web server using Cargo:
cargo build -r
cargo run -r --bin ferron
You can also use
Ferron Forge
to build the web server. Ferron Forge outputs a ZIP archive that can be used by the Ferron installer.

Ferron documentation

Ferron 是一个用 Rust 编写的高性能、内存安全的Web服务器。它具有以下特点：高性能（利用Rust的异步能力）、内存安全、可扩展性（模块化架构）和安全性（注重安全实践和并发处理）。主要组件包括：  
- **ferron**：主服务器。  
- **ferron-passwd**：用于生成用户条目和密码哈希的工具。  

目前，Ferron 仍在开发中，可通过克隆代码库并使用 Cargo 构建和运行：  
```bash  
git clone https://github.com/ferronweb/ferron.git  
cd ferron  
cargo build -r  
cargo run -r --bin ferron  
```  
服务器配置可参考 Ferron 文档。Ferron 使用 MIT 许可证，并欢迎社区贡献。

主要讨论点：围绕Ferron web服务器及其功能、性能、安全性、TLS支持、文档问题以及与其他服务器的比较等方面展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对服务器"快速"定义的看法**：Austin-cheney认为"快速"只是流和管道的问题，与编写语言无关，强调配置简单性和低级别操作（如流和管道）。他还特别提到对TLS证书的厌恶。
• **与Caddy的比较**：DoctorOW认为Ferron可能比Caddy更具扩展性，并且配置不会过于冗长，正在考虑迁移。
• **性能比较**：Password4312提出Rust编写的静态web服务器在TechEmpower测试中表现优异，但这些服务器并非通用目的。同时提到个人使用的Dufs支持文件上传功能。
• **TLS支持的必要性**：Arnath质疑现代web服务器是否仍需内置TLS支持，认为可以在边缘终止HTTPS。
• **对Go语言的看法**：Nottorp认为Go语言是编写服务器的更好选择，具有高性能和内存安全性。

补充讨论：
• **文档问题**：Kapilvt提到文档链接返回403错误，影响使用体验。
• **缺乏Nginx的比较**：No_wizard和Bitbasher质疑为何未与Nginx进行比较，Nginx是极其流行的web服务器。
• **安全性讨论**：Timeflex对Ferron主页上通过curl命令直接导入shell脚本的方式表示安全担忧。
• **内存使用和适用场景**：Tepix关心Ferron在低内存设备（如Raspberry Pi 1）上的适用性。
• **功能需求**：Liveafterlove询问Ferron是否支持DTSL用于WebRTC，指出Nginx目前仅提供补丁支持。

争议焦点：
• **TLS支持的必要性**：Arnath认为TLS应在边缘处理，而Austin-cheney则强烈反对证书的复杂性，显示出对TLS支持的不同看法。
• **性能比较的缺失**：多个评论者提到缺乏与Nginx的直接性能对比，质疑Ferron的真实性能表现。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **迁移意愿**：DoctorOW表现出对Ferron的兴趣，正在考虑从Caddy迁移，显示出Ferron在某些用户群体中的潜在吸引力。
• **个性化推荐**：Password4312根据个人经验推荐了其他工具（如Dufs），提供了实用案例。

总体而言，讨论围绕Ferron的功能实现、性能、安全性及其与其他服务器的比较展开，用户关注点集中在配置简便性、TLS处理和实际性能表现。

data.author: kangfeibo
data.article_summary: Coqui TTS是一款先进的AI文本转语音技术，支持自定义语音创建和多语言功能。用户可以输入任何文本，选择语音和语言，快速生成自然流畅的语音。其主要功能包括快速语音克隆、自定义语音设计、高级语音控制和情感设置、实时语音生成、精确的语音参数调整，以及语音版本管理和比较。该技术适用于AI助手增强、教育内容讲解、游戏角色配音、医疗沟通支持、客服语音解决方案，以及为视障人士提供辅助。Coqui TTS提供高质量的语音合成，支持17种语言，并可用于商业用途和社交媒体平台。

43590570.article_content:
Coqui TTS: Natural Speech Generation
Advanced AI Text-to-Speech Technology with Custom Voice Creation and Multi-Language Support
How It Works
Input Your Text
Enter any text you want to convert into speech - from single sentences to entire paragraphs.
Choose Speaker & Language
Select your preferred speaker voice and target language from our extensive collection.
Generate Speech
Click generate and watch as your text transforms into natural-sounding speech instantly.
Powerful Features for Natural Speech
Rapid Voice Cloning from Short Samples
Coqui TTS offers remarkable voice cloning capabilities, allowing users to replicate voices from just 3-second audio samples. This technology opens up a world of possibilities for personalized voice synthesis.
Custom Voice Creation and Design
With Coqui TTS, users can create and customize their ideal voices. This feature enables the development of unique vocal personas tailored to specific needs or preferences.
Advanced Voice Control and Emotion Settings
Coqui TTS provides granular control over voice characteristics, including pace, emotions, and other vocal nuances. This level of customization ensures that the synthesized speech matches the desired tone and style.
Real-Time Voice Generation
Coqui TTS excels in instant voice synthesis and processing. This real-time capability makes it suitable for applications requiring immediate audio feedback or dynamic content generation.
Precise Voice Parameter Adjustment
Users can fine-tune various aspects of the voice output, including pitch and loudness, on a per-word or per-sentence basis. This feature allows for precise adjustments to achieve the desired vocal performance.
Voice Version Management and Comparison
The system allows users to save different versions of voice performances. This feature is particularly useful for comparing variations and selecting the most suitable output for a given purpose.
Practical Applications and Use Cases
AI Assistant Voice Enhancement
Coqui TTS enables the creation of personal AI companions with natural-sounding voices, enhancing the user experience in smart home devices and digital assistants.
Educational Content Narration
The technology facilitates interactive educational content delivery, making online learning more engaging and accessible to diverse learners.
Video Game Character Voicing
Dynamic character voices and dialogues in video games become more realistic and immersive with Coqui TTS, elevating the gaming experience.
Healthcare Communication Support
In the medical field, Coqui TTS can provide patient support and assistance, offering clear and natural-sounding information and instructions.
Customer Service Voice Solutions
Automated support systems benefit from human-like interaction, improving customer satisfaction and reducing the workload on human agents.
Accessibility Aid for Visual Impairments
Coqui TTS offers voice solutions for users with visual impairments or reading difficulties, making digital content more accessible.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is Coqui TTS?
Coqui TTS is an AI-powered text-to-speech voice synthesis platform that converts written text into natural-sounding speech.
How does Coqui TTS work?
The system uses advanced neural networks to transform text input into natural-sounding speech output.
Is Coqui TTS free to use?
Yes, Coqui TTS is available for free use.
Can I use Coqui TTS audio on social media platforms?
Yes, the audio generated by Coqui TTS can be used on various platforms, including YouTube and TikTok.
What languages does Coqui TTS support?
Coqui TTS supports 17 languages, including: English, Español (Spanish), Français (French), Deutsch (German), Italiano (Italian), Português (Portuguese), Polski (Polish), Türkçe (Turkish), Русский (Russian), Nederlands (Dutch), Čeština (Czech), العربية (ARABIC), 中文 (Chinese), Magyar (Hungarian), 한국어 (Korean), 日本語 (Japanese), Tiếng Việt (Vietnamese).
What makes Coqui TTS different from other TTS services?
Coqui TTS stands out due to its superior voice quality and extensive customization options, offering a more natural and flexible speech synthesis experience compared to many other TTS technologies.
Can Coqui TTS be used for business purposes?
Yes, the voices generated by Coqui TTS can be used for commercial applications, providing businesses with high-quality speech synthesis for various needs.

data.title: The DDA Algorithm, explained interactively
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
这篇文章详细解释了数字微分分析器（DDA）算法在二维光线投射中的应用，特别是在网格方块的遍历中。文章从基本概念开始，首先定义了光线起点（ro）和光线方向（rd），并解释如何通过角度计算光线方向。接着，文章讨论了如何确定光线经过的第一个网格，并通过几何推导展示了如何找到下一个网格块。

文章重点介绍了通过计算光线起点到网格线的距离（lengthX和lengthY）来判断光线先穿过哪个网格。通过使用勾股定理，文章展示了如何计算这些距离，并避免了直接求交点，简化了计算过程。最终，通过比较lengthX和lengthY的大小，算法可以决定光线下一个经过的网格。

文章还提供了可编辑的代码示例，使读者能够互动地理解算法的工作原理。总体而言，这篇文章旨在帮助读者全面理解DDA算法在光线投射中的应用。

The DDA Algorithm, explained interactively
I've written a number of voxel raytracers, and all of them (all the good ones, at least) use the
Digital Differential Analyzer Algorithm
for raycasting. I've only ever "implemented" this algorithm once, by copying a reference somewhere. Since then, I've used and re-used that code. But I have something to admit: I've never really understood how it works. I've seen it
explained well
,
explained poorly
,
explained on video
, and still, I just don't get it. It's one of those geometric algorithms that's hard to wrap your head around, at least for me. But recently, I ran into some issues with a raytracer, and I decided to try to fully understand it. And I made this blog post, for others like me.
All code in this article is editable. Examples will update as you modify them.
DDA, in 2D, is an algorithm that iterates over all of the grid squares intersected by a ray. For those who haven't seen the algorithm, it looks like this:
ro.x
ro.y
rdAngle
If you understand the above, have a nice day :) If not, this article has an explanation.
3Blue1Brown
teaches us that a good way to to explain something is to derive it from scratch. So how would you derive this line drawing algorithm? First, we've got our arguments: the
Ray Origin
ro
, and
Ray Direction
rd
. RD has to be normalized. In this article, we calculate it using an angle, like this:
Let's plot those on a grid.
ro.x
ro.y
rdAngle
The first grid space we need to fill in is pretty simple–it's the grid space that
ro
is in. We can floor ro to get the exact integer space.
ro.x
ro.y
rdAngle
Not super exciting, but an
important step
.
Now, we have to figure out what the
next
grid space is. See if you can guess the answer: move the point and the arrow above and guess where the next grid space would be.
At first glance, you might think it has something to do with
rdAngle
, like if the angle is facing up, then the grid space above the dot should be filled in, if the angle is facing to the right, the one to the right should be filled in, etc.
ro.x
ro.y
rdAngle
But if you
play around with the ray origin
, you'll notice that this quickly falls apart.
We need to take into account the distance from the origin point to the different grid squares. If you've spent some time recently with geometry or a graphing calculator, you might already have figured out that this is actually a
line intersection
problem. If you
reset the above program
, you can see that the ro->rd vector intersects with the lines x = 1 and y = 1. (In this article, we are assuming the center of the grid is the origin.) Let's put those intersections on the screen:
ro.x
ro.y
rdAngle
The yellow dot is the intersection between ro->rd and y = 1, and the green dot is the intersection between ro->rd and x = 1.
Now, let's call the
distance
between ro and the yellow dot lengthY.
Similarly, we can call the distance between ro and green dot lengthX.
Now see that when lengthX is
less
than lengthY, the raycasting line intersects x = 1
before
it intersects y = 1, so the next grid space is the one to the right. Similarly, when lengthY is less than lengthX, the raycasting line intersects y = 1 before it intersects x = 1, so the next grid space is the one above.
ro.x
ro.y
rdAngle
Great! We've taken our
first steps
. Before we move to three squares (can you imagine?!), let's talk about that intersection code.
Importantly, we don't actually need to calculate the intersection points. We only need lengthX and lengthY, which are both distances. For those, we can consult Pythagoras. If we imagine the yellow line above as the diagonal of a right triangle, we can calculate its length using its legs, drawn below as pink and blue.
Also note that we're going to be using ro = {0,0} for a little while, for simplicity's sake :')
The length of the pink line is just 1.
We can calculate the color of the blue line with some basic algebra. We want to find the point where the yellow line (presented in
Slope-intercept form mx+b

data.author: OuterVale
data.article_summary: Sparks是一种用于在文本中创建迷你图（sparklines）的字体，无需代码即可实现。它利用OpenType的上下文替换功能，将数字字符自动转换为迷你图，支持条形、点状和点线三种样式，每种样式有五种粗细变化。数据需转换为0-100的范围。使用时，可以通过CSS在网页中加载字体，或在软件如Microsoft Word、Adobe Illustrator和InDesign中启用"上下文替换"功能以生成迷你图。Sparks兼容多种浏览器和设计软件，适用于桌面和网页设计。

主要讨论点：FF Chartwell 字体及其在不同场景下的应用与优势

不同观点：
• **[cjs_ac]** 提到FF Chartwell并不是一个新出现的工具，而是一个已经存在一段时间的商业产品，并提供了相关链接供参考。这表明该工具在行业内已有一定的历史和知名度。

• **[schobi]** 认为虽然将数据以小型条形图的形式嵌入文本中的想法很有趣，但对这些术语（如“spark”或“sparkline”）不熟悉的人可能会感到困惑。他建议在解释这些概念时应更清晰。

• **[cromulent]** 提供了之前在其他平台上关于类似主题的讨论链接（2017年和2020年），表明这个话题并不是一个新问题，之前已有过相关的讨论。

• **[o1o1o1]** 对在web应用中使用字体解决方案来显示条形图的优点提出质疑，认为简单的CSS解决方案可能更合适，并希望有人能解释字体解决方案的优势。

• **[zeristor]** 提到如果这种方法能在markdown中工作会非常方便，但同时也指出由于markdown解析器的不同，可能无法实现标准化。

• **[dvh]** 对GitHub上的项目缺乏演示图片表示不满，认为这影响了用户对项目的直观理解。

补充讨论：
• **[kazinator]** 的评论被标记为“已标记”，可能表示其评论内容存在问题或与讨论主题不符。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于字体解决方案（如FF Chartwell）在web应用中的实际优势，以及在markdown等环境下的适用性与标准化问题。部分用户对其应用场景和实际效果持怀疑态度。

总结：讨论围绕FF Chartwell字体的使用及其在不同应用场景下的实际效果展开，参与者对其历史、使用方法、优势及局限性提出了不同的看法和建议。

A typeface for creating sparklines in text.
Get the font files
here
. (.zip file, 5.2MB)
To quickly include the fonts in your web page you may wish to use our stylesheet which defines all the font-faces and links to the relevant files hosted on github.
<link href="https://tools.aftertheflood.com/sparks/styles/font-faces.css" rel="stylesheet" />
See it working on our
website
or in one of our interactive notebook examples
A simple usage example
Using Sparks within an SVG
Using javascript to create Sparks code from data
Sparks uses OpenType's
contextual alternates
feature to perform simple replacement operations on numbers. It works on both the desktop and the web where it works without Javascript, though it does require a modern-ish web browser that can make use of OpenType features in text. At the moment it is compatible with Microsoft Word (2010 and later), Apple Pages, Adobe Creative Cloud applications, Chrome 33+, Safari 6+, Firefox 4+, and Internet Explorer 10+. (See:
http://stateofwebtype.com/
for a fuller listing of browser compatibility.)
There are currently three variations:
bars, dots, and dot-lines
(line charts with tiny dots at the joints between segments), each of which has five weight variants.
All three of the variants use a fixed scale of 0–100. If your data only goes to e.g., 10, you'll need to first translate your numbers to be out of 100, otherwise you'll end up rendering an especially tiny chart.
The contextual alternates feature (
calt
) is baked into OpenType and Sparks simply leverages this feature in an unconventional way. It takes strings like
123{30,60,90}456
and outputs a sparkline. The example of
123{30,60,90}456
would have with three datapoints of 30, 60, and 90 framed by 123 and 456. Spaces after the commas will prevent the numbers from being transformed. Numbers outside of the brackets are never transformed.
Using Sparks
On the web
When using Sparks as a webfont you
may
wish to explicitly enable the
calt
feature. Contextual ligatures are enabled by default in most modern browsers but in order to support older browsers you can use the following CSS (example pilfered from Adobe's
Syntax for OpenType features in CSS
page):
.yourClass {
font-variant-ligatures: contextual;
-moz-font-feature-settings: "calt";
-webkit-font-feature-settings: "calt";
font-feature-settings: "calt";
}
For more on this see the example code in the
tests
folder.
In MS Word
If you are using MS Word you need to enable the "Use Contextual Alternates" feature for it to be able to draw the sparklines. You can do that simply by heading to "Format > Font > Advanced" and enabling it.
In Adobe Illustrator
Turn on contextual alternates from the OpenType panel menu (Window > Type > OpenType). Here's a
screenshot
.
In Adobe InDesign
Sometimes contextual alternates are activated by default and sometimes they are not. We have no idea why. Use the OpenType menu to make sure they are turned on, which can be found in the options menu of the character palette (Character > Options > OpenType > Contextual Alternates). Here's a
screenshot
.
How it works: the OpenType code
Inside the font files the code that powers the replacement operation for the
bar
and
dot
variations works like this:
feature calt {
ignore sub zero' comma space;
sub braceleft' zero' braceright' by chart.000;
sub braceleft' zero' comma' by chart.000;
sub zero' comma' by chart.000;
sub zero' braceright' by chart.000;
} calt;
while the code for the
dot-line
variation is a bit more complicated, and looks sort of like this:
@theDots [ dot.000 dot.001 ... dot.100 ];
@linesTo000 [ line.000.000 line.001.000 ... line.100.000 ];
# 100 more those classes, one for each possible position.
feature calt {
lookup dotsIgnore {
ignore sub zero' comma space;
# ... repeat for all 100 other numbers.
} dotsIgnore;
lookup DotsSolo {
sub braceleft' zero' braceright' by dot.100;
# ... repeat for all 100 other numbers.
} dotsSolo;
lookup dotsInitial {
sub braceleft' zero' comma' by dot.000;
# ... repeat for all 100 other numbers.
} dotsInitial;
lookup dotsMiddle {
sub zero' comma' by dot.000;
# ... repeat for all 100 other numbers.
} dotsMiddle;
lookup dotsFinal {
sub zero' braceright' by dot.000;
# ... re

data.title: Trump's Tariff Formula Makes No Economic Sense. It's Also Based on an Error
data.author: Leary
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特朗普政府的关税政策及其潜在影响和动机

不同观点：
• **关税计算公式的合理性**：greaber指出该公式可能不合理，尤其是在处理循环贸易模式时会导致无限关税的问题。croes补充说，政府在计算关税时忽略了服务贸易，仅关注商品贸易，导致基础数据错误。
• **关税对经济的影响**：walterbell引用Stephen Miran的论文，认为关税虽然会带来收入，但如果通过货币调整抵消，则不会带来明显的宏观经济影响，且历史上已有类似案例。DarknessFalls则认为，关税的四倍差异可能是故意设置的，目的是通过市场波动获利，并通过谈判获取政治和经济利益。
• **关税政策的动机**：hayst4ck认为，特朗普的政策如果被视为服务于美国寡头或俄罗斯的利益，就不再令人困惑。ArtTimeInvestor进一步提出，特朗普的主要目标可能是保住权力，不仅限于未来三年，而是更长时间。
• **关税对特定国家和行业的影响**：klooney对莱索托等小国面临的高关税表示同情。qwertox指出，即使美国对华加征高额关税，中国机器人仍可能因成本优势被使用，关税对制造业影响有限。

补充讨论：
• **对特定人物和地区的调侃**：user1241320和renewiltord对文章中提到的马提尼克岛和一些小岛屿进行了调侃，ilrwbwrkhv则讽刺了科技界人物Marc Andreessen可能对关税政策的反应。
• **对政策透明度和误解的讨论**：fblp表示对文章中提到的误差及其可能导致的四倍 inaccuracy不理解，希望有人能用例子解释。

争议焦点：
• **关税政策的合理性与动机**：一部分人认为关税政策存在计算和逻辑上的问题，而另一部分人则从经济和政治动机角度为其辩护，认为关税可能带来收入并服务于特定政治目标。

data.title: 404s – gallery of error 404 page designs
data.author: ChrisArchitect
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为"Footr Design"的网站，该网站精心收集展示各种独特和出色的网页底部设计（footers）。页面列出了多个设计工作室和其作品链接，每个链接附有简要描述和"Gosto!"标签，表示被推荐。设计风格多样，包括3D、动画、黑暗风格、插图、交互式、简洁设计等。部分链接显示"No items found"（未找到内容）。网站为网页设计爱好者提供灵感，展示了不同风格的优秀网页底部设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同的404页面设计及其功能

不同观点：
• [欣赏承认错误的404页面]：spencerflem 认为一些404页面能够坦率承认是自身删除了页面或破坏了链接，而不是暗示用户“迷路”了，这种做法值得赞赏。
• [有趣的404页面设计]：ndr 分享了一个有趣的404页面设计网站（https://www.404s.design/hackernews），展示了一些别出心裁的设计。
• [品牌相关的404页面]：Svip 提到Peugeot的404页面使用了Peugeot 404车型的图片，虽然有趣，但指出并不是每个HTTP状态码都能通过品牌车型来表现。
• [简约404页面设计]：kro 主张404页面设计应尽量简约，减少复杂性，特别是避免不必要的资源浪费，如旧的touch/favicon请求，以节省带宽。
• [公益用途的404页面]：4ndrewl 建议利用404页面做公益，例如通过https://notfound.org帮助寻找失踪儿童，将错误页面转化为有社会意义的工具。
• [文化关联的404页面]：peterburkimsher 提到在新西兰文化中，404这个数字与一个具体地址相关（404 Great South Road, Greenlane, Auckland 1051），将404与地理位置联系起来，增加了讨论的趣味性。
• [幽默的404节日]：ChrisArchitect 以“Happy 404 Day”作结，用幽默的方式看待404错误，将其视为一种“节日”。

补充讨论：
• 404页面的设计不仅仅是技术问题，还涉及到用户体验、品牌展示以及社会公益等多方面的考量。
• 不同用户对404页面的期待和欣赏角度不同，有的人关注页面趣味性，有的人则注重实用性和简约性。
• 一些用户提到了具体的404页面示例，展示了各种设计风格，从品牌关联到公益利用，再到纯粹的趣味设计。

43589119.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为"Footr Design"的网站，该网站精心收集展示各种独特和出色的网页底部设计（footers）。页面列出了多个设计工作室和其作品链接，每个链接附有简要描述和"Gosto!"标签，表示被推荐。设计风格多样，包括3D、动画、黑暗风格、插图、交互式、简洁设计等。部分链接显示"No items found"（未找到内容）。网站为网页设计爱好者提供灵感，展示了不同风格的优秀网页底部设计。
43589119.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同的404页面设计及其功能

不同观点：
• [欣赏承认错误的404页面]：spencerflem 认为一些404页面能够坦率承认是自身删除了页面或破坏了链接，而不是暗示用户“迷路”了，这种做法值得赞赏。
• [有趣的404页面设计]：ndr 分享了一个有趣的404页面设计网站（https://www.404s.design/hackernews），展示了一些别出心裁的设计。
• [品牌相关的404页面]：Svip 提到Peugeot的404页面使用了Peugeot 404车型的图片，虽然有趣，但指出并不是每个HTTP状态码都能通过品牌车型来表现。
• [简约404页面设计]：kro 主张404页面设计应尽量简约，减少复杂性，特别是避免不必要的资源浪费，如旧的touch/favicon请求，以节省带宽。
• [公益用途的404页面]：4ndrewl 建议利用404页面做公益，例如通过https://notfound.org帮助寻找失踪儿童，将错误页面转化为有社会意义的工具。
• [文化关联的404页面]：peterburkimsher 提到在新西兰文化中，404这个数字与一个具体地址相关（404 Great South Road, Greenlane, Auckland 1051），将404与地理位置联系起来，增加了讨论的趣味性。
• [幽默的404节日]：ChrisArchitect 以“Happy 404 Day”作结，用幽默的方式看待404错误，将其视为一种“节日”。

补充讨论：
• 404页面的设计不仅仅是技术问题，还涉及到用户体验、品牌展示以及社会公益等多方面的考量。
• 不同用户对404页面的期待和欣赏角度不同，有的人关注页面趣味性，有的人则注重实用性和简约性。
• 一些用户提到了具体的404页面示例，展示了各种设计风格，从品牌关联到公益利用，再到纯粹的趣味设计。

主要讨论点：提供备用URL的有效性和可信度

不同观点：
• **支持使用备用URL的观点**：
  - 认为提供备用URL（如MSN的链接）有助于访问可能被防火墙阻挡的内容。
  - 例子：一些用户可能无法直接访问某些新闻网站，备用链接提供了替代路径。
  - 论据：MSN等大型门户网站通常比较可信，并且链接可能经过编辑筛选，确保信息的可靠性。

• **质疑备用URL的观点**：
  - 担心备用URL可能导致用户访问到不完整或过时的信息。
  - 例子：新闻内容在不同平台上更新速度不一，可能在转载过程中出现信息滞后。
  - 论据：第三方平台可能对内容进行修改或删减，影响原新闻的完整性和真实性。

• **对信息安全和隐私的关注**：
  - 担心点击未知URL可能会带来安全风险，如钓鱼网站或恶意软件。
  - 例子：有用户提到曾因点击不明链接导致个人信息泄露。
  - 论据：建议在点击任何链接之前，验证其安全性和来源的可信度。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户提到可以利用浏览器插件或工具来验证链接的安全性，并建议在社交平台或论坛上分享链接时附带简短说明或评价，帮助其他用户判断是否值得点击。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，备用URL在不同地区的访问效果可能不同，例如某些链接在一个国家可以顺畅访问，而在另一个国家可能会受到限制。

争议的焦点：备用URL的可靠性和安全性，以及其在不同平台上的信息一致性问题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GW-BASIC源代码及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• [stkai] 认为GW-BASIC源代码中的注释非常有趣，特别是那些幽默的注释，比如关于随机数生成器的警告，提到"不要改变这些常量，除非参考Knuth的第二卷第三章"。
• [nilsbunger] 提到源代码中的一些效果（如字体闪烁）令人分心，并引用Steve Jobs的观点，认为微软缺乏“品味”。不过，他仍然对Bill Gates的公益事业表示赞赏。
• [zabzonk] 从技术角度出发，认为编写BASIC解释器（尤其是带有浮点运算的）非常困难，称赞了Gates和Allen等人在早期开发中的成就。
• [n0rdy] 将阅读源代码比作技术演变的时光机，并提出思考：2025年的代码到2075年是否也会显得过时。

补充讨论：
• [jwnin] 认为早期的PC时代有着无法预料的运气和风险，可能一生只能遇到一次这样的变革时代（如PC、移动电话或互联网的兴起）。
• [jer0me] 提供了源代码的链接，但提醒大家该文件非常大（100 MB PDF）。
• [MrFurious] 和 [-__---____-ZXyw] 都提到网页非常重，导致他们的设备出现问题（如手机冻结、音乐播放卡顿）。
• [_fat_santa] 偏离主题地评论了“Gates Notes”博客，认为它看起来非常独特，不像一般的个人博客。
• [jlmcgraw] 对源代码中的手写笔记感到好奇，提到笔记内容与1975年的时间吻合。
• [azemetre] 提到阅读源代码让他联想到Palo Alto一书，暗示两者之间可能有某种文化或历史上的联系。
• [dr_dshiv] 提到与Bill相关的LSD视频，暗示对Bill Gates早期经历的兴趣。
• [PythonicIT] 表示自己不如其他技术高手，但计划将GitHub上的代码编译到自己的电脑上，展示了一种动手实践的态度。
• [djmips] 提到最近对同一代码的反汇编，并指出部分代码与源代码匹配。
• [keepamovin] 认为文本是一种未被充分利用的设计媒介，对源代码的文本设计表示赞赏。

争议焦点：
- 网页性能问题：一些用户（如MrFurious和-__---____-ZXyw）抱怨网页非常重，导致设备出现问题，而其他用户则未提及此问题。

data.title: The slow collapse of critical thinking in OSINT due to AI
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了开源情报（OSINT）领域中对生成型人工智能（GenAI）工具的过度依赖正导致分析师的批判性思维能力下降。起初，这些工具被用于简单的任务，如总结文档或翻译外文，但逐渐地，分析师开始依赖它们生成线索、撰写报告，甚至不再仔细验证信息的准确性。文章引用了一项2025年的研究，表明对AI的信任度越高，用户的批判性思维就越少，且更倾向于接受AI的输出结果而不加质疑。这种依赖可能导致错误的信息被接受，从而影响OSINT的准确性和完整性。文章警告，若不重新重视批判性思维，OSINT从业者可能会沦为自动化操作员，而非调查员。文章呼吁业内人士警惕这一趋势，并主动保持批判性思维的核心习惯。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生成式人工智能（GenAI）在开放源情报（OSINT）等领域中的应用及其对人类分析和批判性思维的影响。

不同观点：
• **Aurornis**：认为AI并没有让专业人士变得懒惰，这些专业人士过去也依赖其他来源（如播客、新闻文章等）获取意见。AI只是让这种外包思维变得更加便捷。同时，AI让用户感觉聪明，导致他们误以为仍在进行批判性思考。
• **Animats**：强调在信息过载的时代，寻找有价值的信息是主要问题。引用了CIA的OSIRIS系统，指出AI在情报分析中的实际应用，尤其是摘要生成。
• **jruohonen**：指出AI导致用户省略了假设形成、验证来源和多角度评估等关键步骤，直接采用AI的总结，这种现象已经在实际工作流程中出现。
• **sanarothe**：认为动手进行书写、编辑和分析等具体工作过程有助于深入思考和产生新想法。依赖AI可能忽略了这些重要的思维过程。
• **palmotea**：讽刺地指出，AI通过降低人类智力来实现“超人智能”，暗示AI可能让用户变得过于依赖。
• **0hijinks**：质疑AI在实际应用中的效率，认为如果用户最终还是要对AI的结果进行详细验证，那么直接手动完成可能更有效。
• **pcj-github**：分享了个人学习编程语言的经历，认为AI在初期有帮助，但长期依赖可能减缓真正掌握技能的速度。
• **ang_cire**：质疑在OSINT中使用AI的实际效果，认为AI无法替代专业知识和传统方法。
• **LurkandComment**：基于多年分析经验，指出专业分析师具备批判性思维，AI只是提供了新的工具，但数据验证和传统分析方法依然重要。
• **treyfitty**：认为AI在提供基础信息时非常有效，如解释OSINT的定义，节省了用户的时间。
• **ridgeguy**：认为AI的应用不仅限于OSINT，而是在广泛的领域中作为新工具被采用。
• **sepositus**：质疑Aurornis的观点，认为如果专业人士对AI的局限性失去警惕，那是由于懒惰，而不是因为AI的快速和自信响应。
• **BrenBarn**：将AI的应用比作药物成瘾，认为AI的使用方式和其潜在危害值得警惕，尽管文章通常避免直接批评AI。

补充讨论：
• 信息过载问题在情报分析中的重要性，尤其是在历史背景下的演变（如NSA和CIA的案例）。
• 比较多个LLM的输出可能有助于提高信息的可靠性，但同时也提出了生态影响的考虑。

43573465.article_content:
Search
OSINT used to be a thinking game. Now it’s becoming a trusting game and that should terrify you.
I’ve seen it firsthand, analysts running solid investigations, then slowly shifting more and more of the thinking to GenAI tools. At first, it’s small. You use ChatGPT to summarise a document or translate a foreign post. Then it’s helping draft your reports. Then it’s generating leads. And eventually, you’re not thinking as critically as you used to. You’re verifying less, questioning less, relying more.
We tell ourselves we’re “working smarter.” But somewhere along the way, we stop noticing how much of the actual thinking is being offloaded.
This isn’t a rant against AI. I use it daily, ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, Gemini. They’re in my workflow like everyone else’s. But the tradecraft is slipping. Analysts are skipping the hard parts. They’re trusting GenAI to do the heavy cognitive lifting, and it’s changing how we operate at a foundational level.
When OSINT becomes too easy, too efficient, too comfortable… you should be worried. Tradecraft isn’t just about speed, it’s about judgment. And judgment doesn’t come from a language model. If we keep going down this path without pushing back, without actively preserving the critical habits that define our profession, we risk becoming operators of automation instead of investigators.
This blog is a wake-up call. For myself. For anyone working in OSINT. For the people teaching it, and the people just getting started. If we don’t reclaim the thinking side of this game, we’ll lose the game entirely.
The Study That Should Alarm You
In early 2025, a team from Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft Research published something every OSINT analyst should read, but most haven’t. It was a large-scale survey of 319 knowledge workers using GenAI tools like ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, and Gemini in their daily work.
What they found is a warning shot.
The study revealed a clear pattern: the more confidence users had in the AI, the less they thought critically. In contrast, the more confident they were in themselves, the more likely they were to question the output, verify the information, and think deeply about the task.
Let that sink in: Confidence in AI replaces confidence in self and with it, the thinking disappears.
Here’s the punchline:
High trust in GenAI consistently led to reduced critical thinking and less cognitive effort across the board.
Participants weren’t lazy. They were experienced professionals. But when the tool responded quickly, confidently, and clearly they stopped doing the hard part. They stopped questioning. Stopped verifying. Stopped applying the mental friction that separates automation from investigation.
The scary part is that many users still believed they were thinking critically, because GenAI made them feel smart.
The researchers saw a new type of behavior emerge:
•  Instead of forming hypotheses, users asked the AI for ideas.
•  Instead of validating sources, they assumed the AI had already done so.
•  Instead of assessing multiple perspectives, they integrated and edited the AI’s summary and moved on.
This isn’t hypothetical. This is happening now, in real-world workflows. And if you’re in OSINT, you know how dangerous that is.
In our line of work, you can’t afford false confidence. You can’t afford a hallucinated source, a mistranslated post, or a manipulated summary. But the more trust you place in GenAI, without friction, without skepticism, the more you risk exactly that.
The study didn’t focus on OSINT directly. But it doesn’t have to. The findings hit home harder here than anywhere else. Because if we lose critical thinking in this field, we don’t just lose accuracy, we lose integrity.
What This Means for OSINT
In OSINT, we deal in fragments. Nothing is handed to us neatly. We build context from chaos:   tweets, photos, forums, leaks, metadata, satellite images, dead links, weird file names. Every good analyst knows that the work isn’t just collecting data. It’s thinking with it.
That’s what’s at risk.
The
Lee et al. study
wasn’t about OSINT specifically, but it described exactly what’s happening in OSINT shops, government teams, threat intel units, and open-source communities around the world. The creeping shift from thinking to prompting, from analyst to editor. Let’s talk real.
Real-World OSINT Scenarios Affected by GenAI Complacency
Scenario 1: Image Verification
You upload a protest photo into a tool like Gemini and ask, “Where was this taken?” It spits out a convincing response: “Paris, near Place de la République.” It sounds right. You move on.
But a trained eye would notice the signage is Belgian. The license plates are off. The architecture doesn’t match. You trusted the AI and missed the location by a country.
Scenario 2: Person of Interest Profile

43573465.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了开源情报（OSINT）领域中对生成型人工智能（GenAI）工具的过度依赖正导致分析师的批判性思维能力下降。起初，这些工具被用于简单的任务，如总结文档或翻译外文，但逐渐地，分析师开始依赖它们生成线索、撰写报告，甚至不再仔细验证信息的准确性。文章引用了一项2025年的研究，表明对AI的信任度越高，用户的批判性思维就越少，且更倾向于接受AI的输出结果而不加质疑。这种依赖可能导致错误的信息被接受，从而影响OSINT的准确性和完整性。文章警告，若不重新重视批判性思维，OSINT从业者可能会沦为自动化操作员，而非调查员。文章呼吁业内人士警惕这一趋势，并主动保持批判性思维的核心习惯。

主要讨论点：生成式人工智能（GenAI）在开放源情报（OSINT）等领域中的应用及其对人类分析和批判性思维的影响。

不同观点：
• **Aurornis**：认为AI并没有让专业人士变得懒惰，这些专业人士过去也依赖其他来源（如播客、新闻文章等）获取意见。AI只是让这种外包思维变得更加便捷。同时，AI让用户感觉聪明，导致他们误以为仍在进行批判性思考。
• **Animats**：强调在信息过载的时代，寻找有价值的信息是主要问题。引用了CIA的OSIRIS系统，指出AI在情报分析中的实际应用，尤其是摘要生成。
• **jruohonen**：指出AI导致用户省略了假设形成、验证来源和多角度评估等关键步骤，直接采用AI的总结，这种现象已经在实际工作流程中出现。
• **sanarothe**：认为动手进行书写、编辑和分析等具体工作过程有助于深入思考和产生新想法。依赖AI可能忽略了这些重要的思维过程。
• **palmotea**：讽刺地指出，AI通过降低人类智力来实现“超人智能”，暗示AI可能让用户变得过于依赖。
• **0hijinks**：质疑AI在实际应用中的效率，认为如果用户最终还是要对AI的结果进行详细验证，那么直接手动完成可能更有效。
• **pcj-github**：分享了个人学习编程语言的经历，认为AI在初期有帮助，但长期依赖可能减缓真正掌握技能的速度。
• **ang_cire**：质疑在OSINT中使用AI的实际效果，认为AI无法替代专业知识和传统方法。
• **LurkandComment**：基于多年分析经验，指出专业分析师具备批判性思维，AI只是提供了新的工具，但数据验证和传统分析方法依然重要。
• **treyfitty**：认为AI在提供基础信息时非常有效，如解释OSINT的定义，节省了用户的时间。

主要讨论点：电吉他失真的性质、应用及其在音乐中的角色

不同观点：
• Tade0认为电吉他的失真波形通常是锯齿波，只有在琴弦正中拨动时才会接近三角波。他还提到失真的音色受演奏技巧影响，例如拨弦方向，并举例像Mesa Boogie这样的放大器通过利用有限的增益带宽积（GBP）来获得特定的音色。此外，他指出像BOSS DS-1的效果器，新版芯片虽然技术上更优，但因缺少老版芯片的特性而失去了独特的音色。

• Kazinator指出单音失真因电路改进迅速被主流接受，但难听的失真仍被排斥。他认为失真音色丰富，与弓弦乐器和木管乐器有相似之处。尽管有些前卫音乐人会使用难听的失真音色，但这些音色仍属小众。他还讨论了失真音色在复杂和声部分的局限性，并以爵士/摇滚融合为例，说明失真在独奏中的接受度高于和声部分。此外，他强调重金属音乐依赖大量失真，并通过复杂节奏和分层录音创造独特的音色纹理。

• Myself248分享了一个个人理论，认为失真吉他音色类似于发动机声音，象征自由。他通过播放Pink Floyd的音乐让妹妹理解失真的音色。

• Drops引用Brian Eno的话，认为失真是媒介突破极限的标志，许多现代艺术正是通过这些“失败”的音色表达极致的情感与事件。

• Driggs赞赏作者对失真的详细分析，但认为其写作风格过于学术化。他推荐了一段Henry Rollins和Don Was关于失真的对话，认为更具艺术性。

补充讨论：
• 失真音色的技术细节，如波形、增益带宽积对音色的影响。
• 失真音色在不同音乐类型中的应用与接受度，特别是重金属和爵士/摇滚融合。
• 失真作为艺术表达的一部分，其文化和情感意义。
• 学术性讨论与艺术性表达之间的平衡。

data.title: German conservatives sound alarm over gold reserves held in US
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了德国对存放在美国纽约联邦储备银行的黄金储备安全性的担忧。由于美国政治局势不稳定，包括总统特朗普的干预行为和对司法系统的挑战，一些德国政客开始质疑这些黄金是否仍然安全。早在2012年，德国议员Marco Wanderwitz就曾要求检查这些黄金，但未成功。如今，随着美国政治不确定性增加，他再次提出这一问题。欧盟议员Markus Ferber也呼吁对存放在美国的德国黄金进行更多检查。尽管德国央行行长Joachim Nagel表示信任美联储，但过去曾有右翼民粹主义者推动类似检查，导致部分黄金被运回德国。这反映了德国对黄金储备安全的持续关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数字资产的所有权与控制权

不同观点：
• 观点一：数字资产应由用户完全控制。skylurk认为，如果数字资产（如加密货币或NFT）不由用户自己掌控（即私钥或钱包不在用户手中），那么这些资产就不真正属于用户。他引用了传统说法“Not your keys, not your coins”来支持自己的立场，强调去中心化和个人主权的重要性。
  
• 观点二：托管服务有其存在的必要性。一些用户认为，托管服务（如交易所或第三方钱包）为新手或不愿管理自己私钥的用户提供了便利和安全性。这些服务可以降低用户因自身操作失误而导致的资产丢失风险，并且在某些情况下提供保险或赔偿措施。

• 观点三：用户责任与安全意识的平衡。部分讨论者认为，虽然用户应该尽量掌握自己资产的控制权，但现实情况是，很多用户缺乏必要的技术知识或安全意识，容易因操作不当导致资产损失。因此，他们认为在教育用户提高安全意识和使用托管服务之间应该有一个平衡。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于"去中心化"理想与现实操作难度之间的矛盾。一些用户坚持完全去中心化的理念，认为这是区块链技术的核心价值，而另一些用户则关注实际操作中的安全性和便利性。
• 技术门槛问题：一些讨论者提到，私钥管理对于非技术用户来说过于复杂，这是阻碍更多人进入区块链领域的一个重要因素。
• 责任归属问题：如果用户选择使用托管服务并丢失资产，责任应该归属于用户自己还是托管方，这也是讨论中的一个关键点。

43589494.article_content:
Can the United States be trusted with Germany’s gold?
Its leader is trying to
cripple
the country’s most important industry. His deputy thinks it’s a
pathetic freeloader
. The man who has their ear is throwing what look a lot like Nazi salutes and openly
interfering in its elections
to support a far-right party that its own intelligence service thinks is a
threat to the constitution
.
No wonder, then, that some politicians in Germany are worried that what was for decades seen as one of the world’s most reliable storehouses might not be so secure after all.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Germany holds the world’s second-largest gold reserves, and keeps 37 percent of them — some 1,236 metric tons, worth €113 billion — in the vaults of the New York Federal Reserve. Those holdings of precious metal guarantee that, should the need ever arise, the Bundesbank has access to something it can change into U.S. dollars (or any other hard currency).
The very idea that they might not be safe would have been considered ridiculous from 1945 ... until a couple of weeks ago. But the certainties of Germany’s postwar existence have been turned on their head and — as the recent
scrapping
of a notorious cap on public borrowing showed — the unthinkable is suddenly very thinkable indeed. All the more so given evidence of U.S. President Donald Trump’s willingness to push the limits of his powers and assert presidential primacy over the
judicial system
.
German tabloid Bild, owned by POLITICO parent company Axel Springer,
reported
on Thursday that outgoing Christian Democratic Union (CDU) lawmaker Marco Wanderwitz is one of those concerned.
Already in 2012, Wanderwitz had unsuccessfully requested to inspect the gold holdings as part of an effort to pressure the bank to either take a more active role as a custodian, or to repatriate it to Germany.
“Of course, the question now arises again,” Wanderwitz said in comments reported by Bild.
European Union lawmaker Markus Ferber, also of the CDU, equally called for more checks on German gold stored in the U.S.
Advertisement
Advertisement
“Official representatives of the Bundesbank must personally count the bars and document their results,” Bild quoted him as saying.
In the past, the idea that gold stored in official vaults may not be safe has generally been the preserve of cranks and conspiracy theorists. However, it has been revived, ironically, by none other than the billionaire and
éminence grise
of the Trump administration, Elon Musk, who has
called
for an inspection of the U.S.’s own gold reserves.
You do not talk about Bullion Club
For the Deutsche Bundesbank, which is tasked with the safe management of Germany’s most valuable financial asset, the first rule of Bullion Club is you do not talk about Bullion Club, and you most certainly don’t cast aspersions on fellow members.
“We have a trustworthy and reliable partner in the Fed in New York for the storage of our gold holdings,” said Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel during a February press conference, a comment that the bank directed POLITICO back to on Friday. “It does not keep me awake at night. I have complete confidence in our colleagues at the American central bank.”
“We have a trustworthy and reliable partner in the Fed in New York for the storage of our gold holdings,” said Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel | Kirill Kudryavtsev/AFP via Getty Images
However, it’s barely a decade since the Bundesbank was jolted into similar action, when the more immediate public concern was that Germany’s accumulated wealth would be frittered away bailing out the rest of the eurozone.
In 2013, a noisy campaign driven by right-wing populists — which resonated enough with the broader population to embarrass then-Chancellor Angela Merkel — led to the Bundesbank repatriating all of the gold it had previously stored in the Bank of France’s vaults.  At the time, the Bundesbank argued that it no longer needed a means to access foreign currency in Paris, now that Germany and France shared the euro.
Today, over half of the Bundesbank’s reserves are stored on its premises in Frankfurt. Outside the U.S., the remaining 13 percent is held at the Bank of England.

data.title: A university president makes a case against cowardice
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了2025年美国高等教育面临的困境，尤其是在第二次特朗普政府执政下，大学成为针对目标。政府对多样性、公平性和包容性项目展开调查，削减联邦资金，并试图驱逐参与亲巴勒斯坦活动的国际学生。哥伦比亚大学被迫同意政府的多项要求以恢复资金，随后校长辞职。在这种趋势下，许多高校领导者选择谨慎行事，但韦斯利安大学校长迈克尔·罗斯则公开反对政府干预，支持大学应坚持原则。罗斯在处理校内抗议和外部压力时，强调自由言论和参与公共事务的重要性，并批评其他大学以中立为借口避免麻烦。文章还提到罗斯对2024年大选前高校不愿公开支持非党派活动的失望。总体而言，文章反映了当前美国高校在政治压力下的复杂处境和罗斯的坚定立场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国大学在面对政治压力和外部干预时的应对以及其对学术自由和言论自由的影响

不同观点：
• pseudolus和low_tech_love认为大学应保持学术自由和言论自由，不应屈从于政府或捐助者的压力。他们强调，即便接受政府资金，大学也有权自主决定其学术和言论方向，并举例说明个人自由权利的重要性。
• necubi指出，Wesleyan大学在平衡言论自由和提供安全学习环境方面做得较好，但仍担忧美国大学体系可能受损，特别是对外国学生的影响。
• mapt和rtkwe批评哥伦比亚大学和哈佛大学为了资金和回报而屈从于政治压力，认为这些大学背叛了学生，尤其是哈佛拥有巨额资金却未在关键时刻站出来捍卫学术自由。
• mmooss认为超级富豪的捐助者对大学决策有不当影响，并质疑大学董事会是否真的支持自由表达。
• sequoia提出，许多美国人对大学持有敌意，并质疑大学是否能在过去几十年中采取不同做法以获得更广泛的支持。
• hayst4ck强调了对权利教育的重要性，并警告如果政府不保护权利，权利将可能被剥夺，尤其是在威权政权下。
• assimpleaspossi认为当前大学中的抗议多由仍在成长和学习的年轻人发起，质疑他们的成熟度。
• carbocation指出，大学的应对策略与其是否拥有医学中心和NIH资助有关。
• siliconc0w提出大学可以通过拒绝录取或开除支持反教育政策的学生来反击。
• JacobiX通过文学作品联想到过去的抗议活动，并指出当前抗议与那个时代的相似之处。
• insane_dreamer警告，如果大学不开始反击政治干预，整个学术界将受到严重损害。

Last Friday could have passed for a lovely spring day on the Connecticut campus of Wesleyan University. Students with books and laptops dotted a green hillside; flocks of admissions visitors trailed tour guides; baseball season had just begun, and practice was under way. It was almost possible to forget the grim straits of American higher education in 2025.
Colleges and universities have been early targets of the second Trump Administration. In the past month, the Administration has announced it will investigate diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts at more than fifty schools; cut hundreds of millions of dollars in federal funding from such institutions as Johns Hopkins and the University of Pennsylvania; and sought to deport international students involved in pro-Palestinian activism. Columbia received a letter from the federal government issuing demands—which included making changes to discipline and admission policies, and placing the department of Middle East, South Asian, and African Studies under “academic receivership”—to be met as a “precondition” for negotiating the restoration of four hundred million dollars in federal funding. The university agreed to these demands the following week; the week after that, the university’s president resigned.
Columbia’s capitulation was in line with a general trend toward circumspection. The memory of Congress grilling university presidents in 2023 seems to be fresh among leaders in higher ed: few want to risk either their jobs or their budgets by saying the wrong thing. A handful of exceptions have stood out; for example, President Christopher Eisgruber, of Princeton, who wrote a piece for
The Atlantic
about “
The Cost of the Government’s Attack on Columbia
.” (This week, the Administration suspended dozens of grants to Princeton.) But perhaps none has been as voluble or persistent as Michael Roth, who has been president of Wesleyan since 2007.
Roth is a historian and a Wesleyan alumnus who, as an undergraduate, designed a major in the history of psychological theory. His scholarship has dealt with Freud and memory but also colleges as institutions, in books such as “
Safe Enough Spaces
” (2019) and “
The Student: A Short History
” (2023). Recent years have brought an increasingly political thrust to both his writing (for national media and his
presidential blog
) and to his work as president. In 2023, in response to the Supreme Court’s ruling against affirmative action, Wesleyan ended legacy admissions.
When Wesleyan students joined the national wave of protests over the war on Gaza, Roth—who describes himself as a supporter of both free speech and Israel’s right to exist—tangled with student protesters as well as with those who wanted him to shut the protests down. Meanwhile, in interviews and essays, he took administrators at other colleges to task for embracing the principles like those found in the “
Kalven report
”—a 1967 document out of the University of Chicago, which advanced the argument that universities should almost always remain scrupulously neutral. (Such stances were, he told me, “a cover for trying to stay out of trouble.”) As the Trump Administration has ramped up its attacks on the academy, Roth has continued to publish widely, urging fellow-leaders to stand up for their principles. “Release Mahmoud Khalil! Respect freedom of speech!” he concluded in
a recent column for
Slate
, which argued that the Columbia activist’s arrest “should terrify every college president.”
Roth and I met in his office, which is dominated by a round  table where he meets with both students and his cabinet. Wearing Blundstones and polka-dot socks, he was loose-limbed and gregarious, and our conversation (which has been edited for length and clarity) was punctuated by the bright sound of batting from the baseball diamond just outside.
You wrote last year, before the election, that colleges and universities weren’t ready for what was coming. How has the reality compared to your expectations?
It’s much worse than I expected.
I had this idea—alas, it was in 2020, just as
COVID
was happening—that it would be great if colleges and universities took our civic responsibilities more seriously and really incentivized students to participate in the public sphere: work on a campaign, zoning commission, whatever. Rigorously agnostic about what they chose to work on. We found a few hundred schools that agreed in principle and we created a network. Before the 2024 election, we reactivated that group, and this time around, the institutions were much less likely to want to be publicly in support of even something so nonpartisan.

43568655.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了2025年美国高等教育面临的困境，尤其是在第二次特朗普政府执政下，大学成为针对目标。政府对多样性、公平性和包容性项目展开调查，削减联邦资金，并试图驱逐参与亲巴勒斯坦活动的国际学生。哥伦比亚大学被迫同意政府的多项要求以恢复资金，随后校长辞职。在这种趋势下，许多高校领导者选择谨慎行事，但韦斯利安大学校长迈克尔·罗斯则公开反对政府干预，支持大学应坚持原则。罗斯在处理校内抗议和外部压力时，强调自由言论和参与公共事务的重要性，并批评其他大学以中立为借口避免麻烦。文章还提到罗斯对2024年大选前高校不愿公开支持非党派活动的失望。总体而言，文章反映了当前美国高校在政治压力下的复杂处境和罗斯的坚定立场。

data.author: briankelly
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者在个人和工作中使用AI编码工具的积极经验，这些工具帮助其团队提高了生产力和输出质量。尽管一些开发者反馈AI工具不太有效，作者认为资深开发者尤其能从中受益，因为他们的经验和知识有助于更好地利用AI。作者提出了成功使用AI编码的三个关键措施：良好结构的需求、工具based的防护机制和基于文件的关键帧管理。文中以具体项目为例，展示了AI如何独立完成编码任务，如平台问题监控项目，作者甚至在不熟悉Python的情况下，借助AI完成了整个项目。作者鼓励软件开发社区尽早接纳AI技术，以提升工作效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）和AI工具对软件开发的影响及开发者的态度

不同观点：
• **necovek**：对Python项目的代码质量持批评态度，认为由初级工程师编写的代码存在许多设计问题，如日志配置不当和竞态条件。总体认为该项目的代码质量较低。
• **conductr**：作为业余编程爱好者，感到LLM和“氛围编码”削弱了他对创造性编程的热情，认为LLM虽然能生成可用的代码，但剥夺了手动构建的成就感，处于一种心理困境中。
• **JohnMakin**：认为AI工具对减轻身体负担（如腱鞘炎）有帮助，但担忧未来开发技能的退化，尤其对新手开发者面临的挑战感到同情，认为未来可能只有经验丰富的“老手”才能真正理解技术细节。
• **rs186**：不赞成使用LLM生成的代码，认为调试和修正由LLM生成的错误代码耗时且不值得，宁愿自己手动编写代码以求安心。
• **only-one1701**：认为AI在绿地项目（新项目）中表现良好，但在棕地项目（已有项目的维护和扩展）中往往表现不佳，甚至比无用更糟糕。
• **sivaragavan**：强调项目前期规划的重要性，并分享使用Rust进行编译时检查的经验，认为AI生成的Rust代码中的错误有助于提前发现问题。
• **amflare**：担心过度依赖LLM会导致自身开发经验和技能的退化，认为虽然目前能有效利用LLM，但长期来看可能会失去独立编写和判断代码的能力。
• **burntcaramel**：支持LLM的使用，但强调经验丰富的开发者能更好地应对LLM生成的高“意外性”代码，提出测试驱动开发（TDD）可以帮助引导和约束AI生成的代码。
• **yoyohello13**：对AI持积极态度，认为使用Claude CLI能有效分担任务，如编写单元测试，从而提高工作效率，且不影响使用自己习惯的编辑器（neovim）。
• **jonnycoder**：认为AI工具在快速发展，建议开发者通过撰写详细的提示来获得理想的结果，并强调利用AI工具创建个人品牌的重要性，建议开发者通过创建和展示多个小型应用来提升个人影响力。
• **plandis**：在商业环境中使用LLM生成代码存在法律和知识产权问题，担心代码的版权性和公司对生成代码的法律责任，尤其是当使用第三方模型时，公司是否会承担责任。
• **vessenes**：认为当前的LLM工具能将开发者转变为架构师或CTO，但这些工具在实现良好架构方面仍存在不足，且使用过程较为繁琐和令人厌烦，导致开发过程缺乏成就感。
• **Quarrelsome**：认为文章中提到的LLM工具填补了AI在实际开发中的一些空白，尤其在水fall开发模式中表现良好，但过去缺乏合适的工具来实现这种模式。
• **scandox**：享受与人类初级开发者互动的过程，认为这种互动有助于共同成长和构建，而AI工具缺乏这种人性化的体验。
• **hinkley**：对AI工具的当前发展方向持怀疑态度，认为AI并没有解决软件开发中关于代码清晰性和可发现性的关键问题，反而可能增加负担，尤其在依赖大量第三方代码的情况下。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了LLM在绿地和棕地项目中的不同表现，以及在商业环境中使用LLM的法律和知识产权问题。
• 开发者对AI工具的态度各异，有的担忧技能退化，有的则积极利用AI提高工作效率，还有的开发者对使用AI工具缺乏成就感表示不满。
• 强调了经验丰富的开发者在有效利用LLM工具中的重要性，尤其是通过TDD和详细的提示来引导和约束AI生成的代码。

43573755.article_content:
There is a lively discussion about this post over at HackerNews:
https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43573755
I’ve integrated some of the points made there into this article.
Introduction
Over the past few months, I have been experimenting with AI-powered coding tools in both my personal and professional projects. The experience has been overwhelmingly positive, both for me and my team of software engineers at work.
We’ve achieved better results in less time, and in many cases, the quality of our output has significantly improved.
Interestingly, this experience contrasts with the feedback I’ve received from some fellow software developers who report that AI tools aren’t working well for them.
I’m now convinced that AI-assisted software development has the potential to elevate our craft to the next level in terms of productivity. This is why I believe our community should embrace it sooner rather than later — but like all tools and practices, with the right perspective and a measured approach.
My motivation for sharing these experiences and the best practices I’ve identified is to help move the needle forward in terms of AI adoption within the broader software development community — even if realistically, it’s only by some micrometers.
The Current State of AI Coding
My Twitter feed suggests that AI-powered coding tools are already generating significant buzz in a specific niche: non-professional developers who are having great fun building software products. For them, these tools primarily serve as enablers, allowing them to tackle projects they might never have considered without such assistance.
More power to them — it’s exciting to witness their journey of struggles and breakthroughs.
However, this represents just one segment of potential users, and certainly not the only group for whom these tools can provide immense value.
The Senior Developer Advantage
My current conclusion, though preliminary in this rapidly evolving field, is that not only can seasoned developers benefit from this technology — they are actually in the optimal position to harness its power.
Here’s the important part: The very experience and accumulated know-how in software engineering and project management — which might seem obsolete in the age of AI — are precisely what enable the most effective use of these tools.
That’s because while I haven’t found the perfect metaphor for these LLM-based programming agents in an AI-assisted coding setup, I currently think of them as “an absolute senior when it comes to programming knowledge, but an absolute junior when it comes to architectural oversight
in your specific context
.”
This means that
it takes some strategic effort to make them save you a tremendous amount of work
.
And who better to invest that effort in the right way than a senior software engineer?
As we’ll see, while we’re dealing with this new, cutting-edge technology, it is the time-tested, traditional practices and tools that enable us to wield this new capability most effectively.
Three important measures for a successful AI coding session
I’ve identified three critical measures needed when working with AI-assisted coding:
Well-structured Requirements
Tool-based Guard Rails
File-based Keyframing
Before diving into these concepts, let me share some real-world examples of how I’ve used AI in my projects.
I will give examples for two categories of projects: green-field and brown-field.
For both categories, I’ll focus on cases where AI handled the entire implementation, or very nearly so.
While I do sometimes use AI as a “better autocomplete” or as a chat-only companion for general discussions, this article focuses on the “real deal” — where AI tooling operates in an agentic mode and handles all the heavy lifting.
For this, my current tool of choice is
Cursor
, powered by Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 3.7 model. Cursor provides the crucial capability to directly edit all files in a project that require changes, and to execute commands related to the software development process.
Example 1: Platform Problem Monitoring
Cursor and Claude, combined with the expertise areas I’ll discuss below, enabled me to create and fully implement a green-field application:
Platform Problem Monitoring
. You can find the source code at
https://github.com/dx-tooling/platform-problem-monitoring-core
.
The application connects hourly to our ELK stack’s Elasticsearch server, reads the latest error messages, and sends us a well-formatted email summarizing the current state of problems on our web platform:
For more details, check out the
“New project: Platform Problem Monitoring”
post.
In this case all of the implementation logic was written by Cursor/Claude, requiring no manual code intervention from my side.
This is especially noteworthy because I don’t actually know Python. Yes, with 25+ years of software development experience, I could probably write a few lines of working Python code if pressed — but I don’t truly
know
the language. I lack the muscle

主要讨论点：对博尔赫斯的推荐与对其作品与人工智能（LLM）关系的探讨

不同观点：
• [viccis] 强烈推荐博尔赫斯的作品，尤其是《特隆、乌克巴尔、奥尔比斯·特蒂乌斯》这篇故事，并认为博尔赫斯的作品大多短小精悍，易于在短时间内阅读。同时，viccis 从哲学角度讨论了 LLMs 是否能创造出博尔赫斯式的知识，并引用康德的认识论，认为 LLMs 无法生成“先验综合知识”。
• [karaterobot] 提出一个假设：如果对博尔赫斯的生活进行深入了解，是否可能自然地创作出类似其风格的作品，而不是简单地模仿和复述。这引发了对 LLMs 未来创作潜力的思考。
• [101008] 认为博尔赫斯的英文翻译缺乏其原著中的诗意和音乐性，强调阅读原著的重要性。
• [6stringmerc] 提到在狱中阅读萨特的《存在与虚无》，并将萨特与博尔赫斯的哲学思想联系起来，认为 LLMs 若基于萨特的作品进行训练，可能会产生令人不安的逻辑推论，反映人类思想和行为的不足。
• [kouru225] 推荐博尔赫斯的短篇小说《福内斯的记忆》，展示了对其作品的个人喜好。

• [tekacs] 推荐了一篇关于博尔赫斯与人工智能的论文，并提供了相关链接，引导读者进一步探讨。
• [jl6] 将博尔赫斯与人工智能、维基百科、卡夫卡、GPU、密码学等主题联系起来，展示了一种跨领域的思考方式。
• [netsharc] 认为博尔赫斯的某些故事像是对“假设”情景的报告，提出这种风格是对博尔赫斯的致敬。
• [mentalgear] 询问是否有该采访的音频文件，表示希望收听原始采访。
• [david_shi] 引用了博尔赫斯的《阿莱夫》中的一段文字，展示了博尔赫斯作品中丰富的想象力和深邃的哲学思考。
• [integralof5y] 认为博尔赫斯与赫伯特·西蒙的对话并未深入探讨人类与机器智能的关系，但承认与这样的伟人共享时间是令人愉快的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是 LLMs 是否能生成类似博尔赫斯风格的作品，以及是否能创造出“先验综合知识”。
• 对博尔赫斯作品的翻译质量存在不同看法，有人认为英文翻译无法捕捉其原著的诗意和音乐性。
• 博尔赫斯的作品与哲学、人工智能的关系被多次提及，展示了其作品在不同领域的广泛影响和讨论潜力。
• 一些评论者提供了额外的阅读材料和资源链接，鼓励读者进一步探索博尔赫斯与人工智能的相关讨论。

data.title: Public domain technical books published before 1964
data.author: xd
data.article_summary: **Tubebooks.org** 是一个提供技术类书籍在线阅读的网站，目前收录了超过100本、总计4.22 GB的电子书，且仍在缓慢更新。网站专注于收录1964年前出版且未续版权的“真空管时代”电子书籍，其中许多书籍由网友提供。站长由于时间限制，主要依靠他人贡献扫描书籍。网站内容涵盖电气工程、音频、无线电、真空管理论与电路设计、测试与测量、被动元件等类别，书籍多为PDF格式。用户可下载书籍的部分内容预览，全书文件较大，下载需注意。若要转载，需联系站长获取许可。代表书籍包括《Applied Electronics》、《Basic Radio》、《Circuit Theory and Design》等，均为经典电子工程教材。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对旧技术书籍与现代技术书籍写作风格和质量的比较

不同观点：
• [怀旧观点] BlandDuck 认为旧的技术书籍具有独特的魅力，包括语言的直接性、细致的论证以及个人化的风格。这些书籍在技术深度和幽默感方面表现突出，而现代技术书籍往往缺乏这种特质。他提到现代教材可能在教学法上有所欠缺，导致这种差异。

• [具体实例] type0 以一本二战前的无线电电子学书籍为例，说明旧书对普通读者的友好性和写作质量。他强调，就基础概念的解释而言，现代书籍无法与旧书相媲美。

• [赞赏现代资源] dazzawazza 表达了对链接资源中无废话（no bullshit）风格的赞赏，显示出对直接、实用的技术内容的喜爱，尽管没有直接对比旧书。

补充讨论：
• 旧技术书籍的独特魅力被多位评论者提到，尤其是在语言风格和技术深度方面。
• 现代技术书籍被认为在教学法和基础概念解释上有所不足，但也有评论者对现代资源中的直接风格表示赞赏。
• 争议焦点可能在于现代技术书籍是否在质量上逊色于旧书，具体体现在写作风格和教学方法上。

43592003.article_content:
tubebooks.org
home
Technical books online!
4.22 gigabytes and still (slowly) growing!  Over 100 titles!
Preserving the Knowledge of the Ancients?
I've found that most of the technical books published before about 1964 never
had their copyrights renewed, so now are in the public domain.  So I am
endeavoring to digitize and post some selected books relating to the
"vacuum tube age" of electronics here.
Many - maybe over half now - of these books were
scanned by other people and contributed for me to post here.  Many, many
thanks to all the individuals who have helped out with this endeavor.  I
find that I do not have much time to scan books these days - the demands of the
"day job" have increased much over the past few years - so I'm not
doing a lot of scanning myself.  If you have material that you would like
to contribute, please send me an email.
I have checked to the best of my ability to confirm that these works have
expired copyrights and are now
in the public domain.  If you have information to the contrary, please
contact me at:
For information about copyrights and copyright renewals,
look
here
.  Here's a nice, easy copyright renewal
search
tool
.
For more details on how (and why)
I do this, look lower at the
bottom of
this page
.
If you want to post any of these scans on another site,
please contact me for permission before you do... I like to know who is doing
what with these things!  In general I don't have any issues with others
posting the scans that I myself have done (it might save some bandwidth),
although I do appreciate it if you credit the source of the scan.
Beware - some of these files are very big (noted with
red warnings).  If you're on dialup better start a download and go to bed!
The book scans below are
in Adobe Acrobat (PDF) format.  I recommend that if you don't already have
it you download the latest version of Adobe reader.  Some files have
compressed images that may not work correctly with older versions of Acrobat
reader.
For books containing primarily tube data, like Sylvania, GE, and
RCA tube manuals, see the
tube data page
.
Arranged by subject category,
then alphabetically by title.  Note that there is much overlap in the
subjects (e.g., many "radio" books have a thorough treatment of vacuum
tubes, and most general textbooks cover radio and vacuum tubes in some detail).  Use (ctrl-f) in your browser to find a particular book or
author...
On
most books you click on the name of the title to download an introduction (the
first few pages, usually the title through table of contents)  This way you
can see if you're interested before downloading many megabytes of data.

An introductory EE text -

This college-level
electronics text is "designed for the student with only a limited
background in physics and mathematics".  Covers the basics of AC and
DC circuits and radio propagation, then vacuum tubes and circuits that use
them.  Has some information not found on other texts, like high-frequency
and microwave radio, transmission line theory, and DC amplifiers.  Another
good text!

and even servomechanisms.

Most of this book is
dedicated to telephony.  Sections on acoustics and transducers, fundamental

discusses radio communications, mostly as they relate to the telephone system.

A different college EE

and lots of information about motors.  I think this was targeted largely at
Civil, Industrial, and Mechanica

data.title: Recreating Daft Punk's Something About Us
data.author: MistyMouse
data.article_summary:
本文作者在多年后重新尝试使用Ableton Live 12，并决定用它来制作一首翻唱曲，以熟悉软件。他选择了Daft Punk的《Something About Us》作为重制对象，这首歌是法国触碰（French Touch）音乐运动的代表作，该运动源于70-80年代的法国，融合了模拟与数字音效，并受到当时日本电视节目和电子音乐先锋的影响。

作者指出，法国触碰音乐的魅力在于其不完美的质感，这些质感源于当时的设备和录制环境。重现这种音效具有挑战性，因为现代工具过于精确，缺乏原版的粗糙和自发性。在重制过程中，作者选择了类似的音色和处理方式，如使用S.K.Y. Keys插件模拟Wurlitzer电钢琴，并通过简单的处理保持音色的温暖和动感。最终，作者强调，重现经典不仅在于复制音符，更在于捕捉其中的情感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Daft Punk及其音乐创作，特别是专辑《Discovery》的采样和音乐制作技巧，以及AI在艺术创作中的应用。

不同观点：
• [phrotoma] 分享了一系列与Daft Punk及类似电子音乐人相关的经典采样视频，强调了音乐制作中的采样文化，尤其是Daft Punk如何通过采样创造出独特的音乐作品。
• [dan_pixelflow] 对文章中使用生成式AI制作配图表示困惑和不满，认为讨论音乐制作的创造性不应与反创造性的AI生成内容并存。这一观点引发了对AI在艺术创作中角色的讨论。
• [hnlmorg] 强调了Daft Punk的《Discovery》专辑中大量使用采样的特点，并指出文章忽略了这一点，同时提到专辑中贯穿的动画故事也是亮点。
• [KaiserPro] 表达了对音乐制作分解视频的喜爱，并推荐了一个相关的音乐播客，但未深入讨论采样或AI相关问题，更多是从音乐制作工具和历史角度出发。
• [dash2] 分享了Prodigy的《Smack My Bitch Up》的 recreation 视频，强调了这种音乐分析所需的高水平音乐知识。
• [nakedneuron] 强调了Daft Punk音乐在记忆中的根深蒂固，并提出了对AI在未来音乐分析和再创造中应用的展望。
• [lxgr] 推荐了与Daft Punk和70/80年代动画美学相关的电影《Interstella 5555》，将音乐与视觉艺术结合讨论。
• [hnlurker22] 分享了一个Theremin（特雷门琴）的翻唱视频，从一种独特的乐器角度参与讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[dan_pixelflow] 提出的AI生成内容与艺术创作的矛盾，即在讨论音乐制作创造性的文章中使用AI生成内容是否合适，引发了对AI在艺术领域角色的思考。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：[simian1983] 意外地提到了对文本编辑器BBEdit的支持，虽然与主要讨论点无关，但显示了讨论中的多样性。
• 情感因素：[squigz] 表达了对Daft Punk解散的悲伤情感，显示了音乐艺术家对粉丝的深远影响。

总结：评论主要围绕Daft Punk的音乐创作和采样技巧展开，同时涉及AI在艺术创作中的角色争议，以及对具体音乐作品和工具的推荐与分享。

43591050.article_content:
Marca Tatem
— San Francisco, April 3rd, 2025
After years of finding it confusing and unintuitive, I finally gave
Ableton Live
another shot. With
version 12
(current as of this writing), it feels significantly more refined—so much so that it's officially become my DAW of choice.
When learning a new music production software, recreating a cover track is always a smart move. You don't have to worry too much about the songwriting itself, which frees you up to focus on the tools and the production process.
For this project, I picked a track that's emblematic of the
French Touch
movement and now nearing its 25th anniversary:
Daft Punk's
Something About Us
. Rebuilding it in a modern production environment turned out to be trickier than I expected, but here's how it went, track by track.
Wait... What's the French Touch, Anyway?
To me,
French Touch
isn't just a genre—it's a
cultural artifact
born from a very specific time and place: France in the late
'70s
and
'80s
. Its distinct sound is the product of a generation raised on
analog dreams of the digital future
.
These artists—
Daft Punk
,
Justice
,
Kavinsky
, and others—grew up immersed in a bizarre and colorful media landscape. Japanese TV shows like
X-OR
,
Sankukai
, and
Albator 84
filled French screens with space corsairs, robotic heroes, and mythological remixes set in futuristic worlds. Their themes were packed with synths, arpeggiators, and digitized voices—sounds that now echo, with a grown-up edge, in the textures of
French Touch
music.
At the same time, France was pushing into the future: science museums, open-air
electronic concerts by pioneers like
Jean-Michel Jarre
, and a sense that the 21st century was just around the corner. Yet beneath that techno-utopian veneer, cities like Paris remained gritty and raw. That tension—between the shiny and the grimy—runs deep in the DNA of
French Touch
. You hear it, especially in the darker, distorted edges of
Justice
and
Kavinsky
.
Let's also not forget the artists who laid the groundwork long before the
French Touch
became a thing. Quirky French electronic pioneers like
Jacno
, the retro-futurist charm of
Telex
from Belgium, and, of course,
Giorgio Moroder
, the godfather of
Italo Disco
—all contributed textures, tones, and sensibilities that would echo decades later. Even mainstream pop acts like
Lio
,
Étienne Daho
, or the orchestral-synth hybrids of
Rondo Veneziano
were constantly spinning on French FM radio, which in the '80s was a chaotic, genre-blurring space. This eclectic mix quietly wired an entire generation of young listeners with an appetite for melody, groove, and synthetic textures—key ingredients in what would later become
French Touch
.
Outrun never looked as good as in your dreams
There's also a certain
California dreamin
g that runs through much of
French Touch
. The imagery of Los Angeles—
endless boulevards flanked by towering palm trees and that golden sunset light
—is a romanticized vision of America that influenced the aesthetic, especially in later works. This fusion of European electronic sensibilities with American dream imagery created something uniquely transportive.
What started as a movement became a signature sound:
nostalgic, futuristic, cinematic, dirty, emotional.
Why It Was So Hard to Recreate
Part of what makes
French Touch
so compelling is also what makes it hard to replicate today. Those
lush, imperfect textures
weren't just stylistic choices—they were the natural result of a specific time, place, and set of tools. Many of these tracks were recorded in a single take, often in cramped Parisian apartments or modest studios, using vintage analog gear and early digital samplers.
There's a rawness and spontaneity to that process. The
hiss of a dusty synth
, the
unquantized groove of a looped disco break
, the warmth of
tape compression
—all of it baked into the DNA of those tracks. Today’s high-resolution digital tools are often too clean, too precise. When you remove the imperfections, you also risk scrubbing out the soul.
The Ableton Live's session
So when I set out to recreate
Something About Us
using modern software, I knew that recreating this track would be more than just copying notes or layering samples—I’d have to
chase a feeling
.
The Keys
In the original track, the keyboard part is likely played on a
Wurlitzer
electric piano
—its
signature bite and warmth
are unmistakable. For my version, I opted for something slightly different: a warmer, more rounded tone using the excellent
S.K.Y. Keys plugin
, specifically the
Everything Right
preset. It doesn't try to mimic the original exactly but brings a vibe that fits the song's emotional core.
I kept the processing minimal: just a gentle midrange boost (mainly to make the part shine a bit more on
AirPods
), a touch of Ableton's stock
Vinyl Distortion
for added warmth, and
side-chain compression
tied to the kick for subtle movement in the mix. After the intro section, I remove the bass note from the keys to carve out space for
43591050.article_summary:
本文作者在多年后重新尝试使用Ableton Live 12，并决定用它来制作一首翻唱曲，以熟悉软件。他选择了Daft Punk的《Something About Us》作为重制对象，这首歌是法国触碰（French Touch）音乐运动的代表作，该运动源于70-80年代的法国，融合了模拟与数字音效，并受到当时日本电视节目和电子音乐先锋的影响。

作者指出，法国触碰音乐的魅力在于其不完美的质感，这些质感源于当时的设备和录制环境。重现这种音效具有挑战性，因为现代工具过于精确，缺乏原版的粗糙和自发性。在重制过程中，作者选择了类似的音色和处理方式，如使用S.K.Y. Keys插件模拟Wurlitzer电钢琴，并通过简单的处理保持音色的温暖和动感。最终，作者强调，重现经典不仅在于复制音符，更在于捕捉其中的情感。

data.title: Nebula Sans
data.author: xucheng
data.article_summary: Nebula Sans是一款现代、人文主义的无衬线字体，专为数字和印刷应用的易读性设计，基于Paul D. Hunt为Adobe Fonts设计的Source Sans。作为Nebula流媒体服务的品牌字体，Nebula Sans可作为Whitney SSm的替代品，并根据SIL开放字体许可证供免费使用。该字体提供两种样式和六种粗细，适合界面、印刷及其他多种用途。其设计初衷包括个性化、集成高级排版功能及降低商业字体许可成本。Nebula Sans在标点、风格替代及表格数字支持等方面对Source Sans进行了调整，以更好地匹配Whitney SSm。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：字体设计及其版权、字体的视觉和功能特点、免费与付费字体的对比

不同观点：
• [eps] 认为 Whitney 是一个独特且美丽的字体，但因 Hoefler 未确认共同拥有权并踢出了联合创始人 Tobias Frere-Jones，Hoefler 是“混蛋”，因此 Whitney 的免费克隆是应得的。
• [jofzar] 分享了一个关于字体数字化和版权知识的视频，并提到了一些技术细节（如 tabular-nums）。
• [lelandfe] 认为这个免费字体只是对 Whitney 做了一些调整，并提到 Source Sans 是其基础，但主要的区别在于是否需要付费。
• [davedx] 讨论了当前“中性美学”的流行趋势，虽然这种风格提供了高度可读的界面，但他怀念早期网络的混乱和活力。
• [sen] 认为该字体的营销努力与其实际创新（只是对现有字体进行了一些拉伸）不成比例。
• [anotheryou] 通过对比图指出 Whitney 看起来干净且连贯，而 Nebula Sans 则显得缺乏个性。
• [delta_p_delta_x] 详细分析了该字体与 Source Sans 的相似性，认为它不值得拥有新名字，并表达了对免费字体质量的普遍不满，强调了付费字体的价值。
• [nucleogenesis] 并不是字体爱好者，但觉得这个字体看起来很时尚，并打算将其作为默认字体。
• [dejongh] 认为字体选择是增加文本美感的重要方式，设计师应该更多地利用这个机会。
• [codedokode] 支持更多自由可用字体，但希望看到字体在小尺寸下的表现，并通过开发工具进行了测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 Hoefler 和 Frere-Jones 的创始权纠纷，以及免费字体与付费字体之间的质量对比。
• 一些用户关注字体的技术特性（如 tabular-nums）和实际应用效果（如小尺寸下的可读性）。
• 对当前设计趋势（如中性美学）的看法不同，有人怀念过去的设计风格，有人接受当前的简洁风格。
• 对字体创新和营销策略的批评，认为一些新字体只是对现有设计的微调。
• 对免费字体和付费字体的详细比较，强调了高质量字体设计所需的巨大努力和成本。

43591225.article_content:
Introducing
Nebula
Sans
A versatile, modern, humanist sans-serif with a neutral aesthetic, designed for legibility in both digital and print applications.
Based on
Source Sans
by Paul D. Hunt for Adobe Fonts.
Nebula Sans is the new brand typeface for
Nebula
, the premium streaming service from independent creators. Based on
Source Sans
and designed to be a drop-in alternative to
Whitney SSm
, Nebula Sans is available for anyone to use under the SIL Open Font License.
Watch our short documentary film about the story behind Nebula Sans, written & directed by David Friedman.
Featuring two styles in six weights, Nebula Sans is well-suited for use in interfaces, print, and for any other graphical, digital, physical, metaphysical, metaphorical, or allegorical typeface needs.
Download
View font license
Nebula Sans Light
Iâd take the awe of understanding over the awe of ignorance any day
Nebula Sans Book
The âtvâ in nebula.tv stands for âTaylorâs Versionâ

Enter the Snack Zone

Thereâs no place like home
